<DIV style="PADDING-LEFT: 0%; PADDING-RIGHT: 0%">

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=2 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>Market leadership changes in unpredictable ways; that&#8217;s one of the reasons why Vanguard believes broad diversification is the wisest choice for many investors.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=2 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>In terms of the funds&#8217; holdings, shares of retailers and other companies closely tied to discretionary consumer spending buoyed the returns of all four funds. These stocks benefited from healthy consumer confidence that, in turn, was fed by </FONT><FONT size=2 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>continued improvements in the U.S. job market. Falling gas prices also made it easier for consumers to open their wallets for everything from clothing to entertainment.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=2 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>Conversely, all four funds experienced steep slides in their returns from energy companies. These stocks were hurt in the second half by a precipitous drop in oil prices.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=2 face=UniversLTStd,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif><STRONG>Over the decade just ended, the funds outpaced their peers</STRONG></FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=2 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>For the ten years ended December 31, the Extended Market Index Fund posted an average annual return of 9.08% and the Mid-Cap Index Fund 9.34%. Since launching in 2006, the Mid-Cap Growth Index Fund has returned an annual average of 9.15% and the Mid-Cap Value Index Fund 9.02%. In each case, the results exceeded the average annual returns of peers.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=2 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>All four funds have closely tracked their target indexes. This is a tribute to the expertise of the funds&#8217; advisor, Vanguard Equity Investment Group, and its team of seasoned professionals. With its sophisticated and proven portfolio management strategies, the group has been able to produce benchmark-tracking returns over the years regardless of market conditions. The advisor is helped in this task by the funds&#8217; low expenses.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=2 face=UniversLTStd,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif><STRONG>Vanguard&#8217;s outlook for investors: Expect less and stay balanced</STRONG></FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=2 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>In Vanguard&#8217;s recently published market outlook, global chief economist Joe Davis and his team discuss expected returns for various asset classes over the coming years. Although not bearish, our outlook on global stocks and bonds is the most guarded since 2006. The report cautions that, over the next decade, returns for a balanced portfolio are likely to be moderately below long-run historical averages.</FONT></P><FONT size=2>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>Our simulations indicate that the average annualized returns of a 60% equity/40% bond portfolio for the decade ending 2024 are most likely to be centered in the 3%&#8211;5% range after inflation, below the actual average after-inflation return of 5.6% for the same portfolio since 1926.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>Even so, Vanguard firmly believes that the principles for investing success&#8212;focusing on clear goals, a suitable asset allocation, low costs, and long-term discipline&#8212;remain unchanged.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>For more information about our expectations and the probability of various outcomes, see </FONT><FONT face=UniversLTStd-LightObl,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>Vanguard&#8217;s Economic and Investment Outlook</FONT><FONT face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>, available at vanguard.com/research.</FONT></P></FONT>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Cn,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>IMPORTANT: The projections and other information generated by the Vanguard Capital Markets Model (VCMM) regarding the likelihood of various investment outcomes are hypothetical in nature, do not reflect actual investment results, and are not guarantees of future results. Distribution of return outcomes from VCMM, derived from 10,000 simulations for U.S. equity returns and fixed income returns. Simulations as of September 30, 2014. Results from the model may vary with each use and over time. For more information, please see page 9.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=2 face=UniversLTStd,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif><STRONG>To build for the long term, start with a solid foundation</STRONG></FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=2 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>As the leader of a major investment firm, I get asked a lot of questions on all kinds of topics, from the outlook for global markets to the best fund choices for an IRA. But a topic that almost never comes up&#8212;and one that I consider perhaps the most important&#8212;is setting investment goals.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=2 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>At Vanguard, we believe that following four timeless, straightforward principles can help put you on the right track toward investment success:</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=2 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>&#8226; </FONT><FONT size=2 face=UniversLTStd,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>Goals. </FONT><FONT size=2 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>Create clear, appropriate </FONT><FONT size=2 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>investment goals.</FONT><BR><BR><FONT size=2 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>&#8226; </FONT><FONT size=2 face=UniversLTStd,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>Balance. </FONT><FONT size=2 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>Develop a suitable asset </FONT><FONT size=2 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>allocation using broadly diversified funds.</FONT><BR><BR><FONT size=2 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>&#8226; </FONT><FONT size=2 face=UniversLTStd,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>Cost. </FONT><FONT size=2 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>Minimize cost.</FONT><BR><BR><FONT size=2 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>&#8226; </FONT><FONT size=2 face=UniversLTStd,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>Discipline. </FONT><FONT size=2 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>Maintain perspective and </FONT><FONT size=2 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>long-term discipline.</FONT><BR><FONT size=2 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=2 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>All four principles are essential, and the </FONT><FONT size=2 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>order in which they&#8217;re listed is intentional. </FONT><FONT size=2 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>Every good investment plan begins with </FONT><FONT size=2 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>a clearly defined goal, which sets the </FONT><FONT size=2 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>foundation for building your portfolio.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Cn,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>IMPORTANT: The projections and other information generated by the Vanguard Capital Markets Model regarding the likelihood of various investment outcomes are hypothetical in nature, do not reflect actual investment results, and are not guarantees of future results. VCMM results will vary with each use and over time.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-LightCn,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>The VCMM projections are based on a statistical analysis of historical data. Future returns may behave differently from the historical patterns captured in the VCMM. More important, the VCMM may be underestimating extreme negative scenarios unobserved in the historical period on which the model estimation is based.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-LightCn,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>The Vanguard Capital Markets Model</FONT><SUP><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-LightCn,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>&#174; </FONT></SUP><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-LightCn,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>is a proprietary financial simulation tool developed and maintained by Vanguard&#8217;s primary investment research and advice teams. The model forecasts distributions of future returns for a wide array of broad asset classes. Those asset classes include U.S. and international equity markets, several maturities of the U.S. Treasury and corporate fixed income markets, international fixed income markets, U.S. money markets, commodities, and certain alternative investment strategies. The theoretical and empirical foundation for the Vanguard Capital Markets Model is that the returns of various asset classes reflect the compensation investors require for bearing different types of systematic risk (beta). At the core of the model are estimates of the dynamic statistical relationship between risk factors and asset returns, obtained from statistical analysis based on available monthly financial and economic data from as early as 1960. Using a system of estimated equations, the model then applies a Monte Carlo simulation method to project the estimated interrelationships among risk factors and asset classes as well as uncertainty and randomness over time. The model generates a large set of simulated outcomes for each asset class over several time horizons. Forecasts are obtained by computing measures of central tendency in these simulations. Results produced by the tool will vary with each use and over time.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=2 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>Setting an investment goal doesn&#8217;t have to be complicated. It can be as simple as saving for retirement or for a child&#8217;s college education. Being realistic about your goals&#8212;and how to meet them&#8212;can help you stick with your investment plan even when times get tough.</FONT></P>

<DIV style="PADDING-LEFT: 0%; PADDING-RIGHT: 0%">

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>Extended Market Index Fund</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=3 face=UniversLTStd,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif><STRONG>Notes to Financial Statements</STRONG></FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>Vanguard Extended Market Index Fund is registered under the Investment Company Act of 1940 as an open-end investment company, or mutual fund. The fund offers five classes of shares: Investor Shares, Admiral Shares, Institutional Shares, Institutional Plus Shares, and ETF Shares. Investor Shares are available to any investor who meets the fund&#8217;s minimum purchase requirements. Admiral Shares, Institutional Shares, and Institutional Plus Shares are designed for investors who meet certain administrative, service, and account-size criteria. ETF Shares are listed for trading on NYSE Arca; they can be purchased and sold through a broker. Prior to October 24, 2014, the fund offered Signal Shares. Effective October 24, 2014, the Signal Shares were converted to Admiral Shares.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>A. </FONT><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>The following significant accounting policies conform to generally accepted accounting principles for U.S. investment companies. The fund consistently follows such policies in preparing its financial statements.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>1. Security Valuation: Securities are valued as of the close of trading on the New York Stock Exchange (generally 4 p.m., Eastern time) on the valuation date. Equity securities are valued at the latest quoted sales prices or official closing prices taken from the primary market in which each security trades; such securities not traded on the valuation date are valued at the mean of the latest quoted bid and asked prices. Securities for which market quotations are not readily available, or whose values have been materially affected by events occurring before the fund&#8217;s pricing time but after the close of the securities&#8217; primary markets, are valued by methods deemed by the board of trustees to represent fair value. Investments in Vanguard Market Liquidity Fund are valued at that fund&#8217;s net asset value. Temporary cash investments acquired over 60 days to maturity are valued using the latest bid prices or using valuations based on a matrix system (which considers such factors as security prices, yields, maturities, and ratings), both as furnished by independent pricing services. Other temporary cash investments are valued at amortized cost, which approximates market value.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>2. Futures Contracts: The fund uses index futures contracts to a limited extent, with the objectives of maintaining full exposure to the stock market, enhancing returns, maintaining liquidity, and minimizing transaction costs. The fund may purchase futures contracts to immediately invest incoming cash in the market, or sell futures in response to cash outflows, thereby simulating a fully invested position in the underlying index while maintaining a cash balance for liquidity. The fund may seek to enhance returns by using futures contracts instead of the underlying securities when futures are believed to be priced more attractively than the underlying securities. The primary risks associated with the use of futures contracts are imperfect correlation between changes in market values of stocks held by the fund and the prices of futures contracts, and the possibility of an illiquid market. Counterparty risk involving futures is mitigated because a regulated clearinghouse is the counterparty instead of the clearing broker. To further mitigate counterparty risk, the fund trades futures contracts on an exchange, monitors the financial strength of its clearing brokers and clearinghouse, and has entered into clearing agreements with its clearing brokers. The clearinghouse imposes initial margin requirements to secure the fund&#8217;s performance and requires daily settlement of variation margin representing changes in the market value of each contract.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>Futures contracts are valued at their quoted daily settlement prices. The aggregate settlement values of the contracts are not recorded in the Statement of Net Assets. Fluctuations in the value of the contracts are recorded in the Statement of Net Assets as an asset (liability) and in the Statement of Operations as unrealized appreciation (depreciation) until the contracts are closed, when they are recorded as realized futures gains (losses).</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>28</FONT></P></DIV>

<DIV style="PAGE-BREAK-BEFORE: always">&nbsp;</DIV>

<!--$$/page=--><A name="page_164"></A><BR>

<DIV style="PADDING-LEFT: 0%; PADDING-RIGHT: 0%">

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>Extended Market Index Fund</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>During the year ended December 31, 2014, the fund&#8217;s average investments in long and short futures contracts represented less than 1% and 0% of net assets, respectively, based on the average of aggregate settlement values at each quarter-end during the period.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>3. Federal Income Taxes: The fund intends to continue to qualify as a regulated investment company and distribute all of its taxable income. Management has analyzed the fund&#8217;s tax positions taken for all open federal income tax years (December 31, 2011&#8211;2014), and has concluded that no provision for federal income tax is required in the fund&#8217;s financial statements.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>4. Distributions: Distributions to shareholders are recorded on the ex-dividend date.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>5. Securities Lending: To earn additional income, the fund lends its securities to qualified institutional borrowers. Security loans are required to be secured at all times by collateral in an amount at least equal to the market value of securities loaned. Daily market fluctuations could cause the value of loaned securities to be more or less than the value of the collateral received. When this occurs, the collateral is adjusted and settled on the next business day. The fund further mitigates its counterparty risk by entering into securities lending transactions only with a diverse group of prequalified counterparties, monitoring their financial strength, and entering into master securities lending agreements with its counterparties. The master securities lending agreements provide that, in the event of a counterparty&#8217;s default (including bankruptcy), the fund may terminate any loans with that borrower, determine the net amount owed, and sell or retain the collateral up to the net amount owed to the fund; however, such actions may be subject to legal proceedings. While collateral mitigates counterparty risk, in the absence of a default the fund may experience delays and costs in recovering the securities loaned. The fund invests cash collateral received in Vanguard Market Liquidity Fund, and records a liability in the Statement of Net Assets for the return of the collateral, during the period the securities are on loan. Securities lending income represents fees charged to borrowers plus income earned on invested cash collateral, less expenses associated with the loan.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>6. Credit Facility: The fund and certain other funds managed by The Vanguard Group participate in a $2.</FONT><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>8</FONT><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>9 billion committed credit facility provided by a syndicate of lenders pursuant to a credit agreement that may be renewed annually; each fund is individually liable for its borrowings, if any, under the credit facility. Borrowings may be utilized for temporary and emergency purposes, and are subject to the fund&#8217;s regulatory and contractual borrowing restrictions. The participating funds are charged administrative fees and an annual commitment fee of 0.06% of the undrawn amount of the facility; these fees are allocated to the funds based on a method approved by the fund&#8217;s board of trustees and included in Management and Administrative expenses on the fund&#8217;s Statement of Operations. Any borrowings under this facility bear interest at a rate equal to the higher of the federal funds rate or LIBOR reference rate plus an agreed-upon spread.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>The fund had no borrowings outstanding at December 31, 2014, or at any time during the period then ended.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>7</FONT><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>. Other: Dividend income is recorded on the ex-dividend date. Interest income includes income distributions received from Vanguard Market Liquidity Fund and is accrued daily. Premiums and discounts on debt securities purchased are amortized and accreted, respectively, to interest income over the lives of the respective securities. Security transactions are accounted for on the date securities are bought or sold. Costs used to determine realized gains (losses) on the sale of investment securities are those of the specific securities sold.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>E. </FONT><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>Distributions are determined on a tax basis and may differ from net investment income and realized capital gains for financial reporting purposes. Differences may be permanent or temporary. Permanent differences are reclassified among capital accounts in the financial statements to reflect their tax character. Temporary differences arise when certain items of income, expense, gain, or loss are recognized in different periods for financial statement and tax purposes. These differences will reverse at some time in the future. Differences in classification may also result from the treatment of short-term gains as ordinary income for tax purposes.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>Certain of the fund&#8217;s investments are in securities considered to be passive foreign investment companies, for which any unrealized appreciation and/or realized gains are required to be included in distributable net income for tax purposes. Passive foreign investment companies held at December 31, 2014, had unrealized appreciation of $6,240,000, of which $4,955,000 has been distributed and is reflected in the balance of overdistributed net investment income.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>During the year ended December 31, 2014, the fund realized $1,696,662,000 of net capital gains resulting from in-kind redemptions&#8212;in which shareholders exchanged fund shares for securities held by the fund rather than for cash. Because such gains are not taxable to the fund, and are not distributed to shareholders, they have been reclassified from accumulated net realized losses to paid-in capital.</FONT></P>

<P style="text-align: left;">
<FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">Mid-Cap Index Fund</FONT></P>
<P style="text-align: left;">
<FONT size=3 face="UniversLTStd,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">Notes to Financial Statements</FONT></P>
<P style="text-align: left;">
<FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">Vanguard Mid-Cap Index Fund is registered under the Investment Company Act of 1940 as an open-end investment company, or mutual fund. The fund offers five classes of shares: Investor Shares, Admiral Shares, Institutional Shares, Institutional Plus Shares, and ETF Shares. Investor Shares are available to any investor who meets the fund&#146;s minimum purchase requirements. Admiral Shares, Institutional Shares, and Institutional Plus Shares are designed for investors who meet certain administrative, service, and account-size criteria. ETF Shares are listed for trading on NYSE Arca; they can be purchased and sold through a broker. Prior to October 24, 2014, the fund offered Signal Shares. Effective at the close of business on October 24, 2014, the Signal Shares were converted to Admiral Shares.</FONT></P>
<P style="text-align: left;">
<FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">A. </FONT><FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">The following significant accounting policies conform to generally accepted accounting principles for U.S. investment companies. The fund consistently follows such policies in preparing its financial statements.</FONT></P>
<P style="text-align: left;">
<FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">1. Security Valuation: Securities are valued as of the close of trading on the New York Stock Exchange (generally 4 p.m., Eastern time) on the valuation date. Equity securities are valued at the latest quoted sales prices or official closing prices taken from the primary market in which each security trades; such securities not traded on the valuation date are valued at the mean of the latest quoted bid and asked prices. Securities for which market quotations are not readily available, or whose values have been materially affected by events occurring before the fund&#146;s pricing time but after the close of the securities&#146; primary markets, are valued by methods deemed by the board of trustees to represent fair value. Investments in Vanguard Market Liquidity Fund are valued at that fund&#146;s net asset value. Temporary cash investments acquired over 60 days to maturity are valued using the latest bid prices or using valuations based on a matrix system (which considers such factors as security prices, yields, maturities, and ratings), both as furnished by independent pricing services. Other temporary cash investments are valued at amortized cost, which approximates market value.</FONT></P>
<P style="text-align: left;">
<FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">2. Futures Contracts: The fund uses index futures contracts to a limited extent, with the objectives of maintaining full exposure to the stock market, enhancing returns, maintaining liquidity, and minimizing transaction costs. The fund may purchase futures contracts to immediately invest incoming cash in the market, or sell futures in response to cash outflows, thereby simulating a fully invested position in the underlying index while maintaining a cash balance for liquidity. The fund may seek to enhance returns by using futures contracts instead of the underlying securities when futures are believed to be priced more attractively than the underlying securities. The primary risks associated with the use of futures contracts are imperfect correlation between changes in market values of stocks held by the fund and the prices of futures contracts, and the possibility of an illiquid market. Counterparty risk involving futures is mitigated because a regulated clearinghouse is the counterparty instead of the clearing broker. To further mitigate counterparty risk, the fund trades futures contracts on an exchange, monitors the financial strength of its clearing brokers and clearinghouse, and has entered into clearing agreements with its clearing brokers. The clearinghouse imposes initial margin requirements to secure the fund&#146;s performance and requires daily settlement of variation margin representing changes in the market value of each contract.</FONT></P>
<P style="text-align: left;">
<FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">Futures contracts are valued at their quoted daily settlement prices. The aggregate settlement values of the contracts are not recorded in the Statement of Net Assets. Fluctuations in the value of the contracts are recorded in the Statement of Net Assets as an asset (liability) and in the Statement of Operations as unrealized appreciation (depreciation) until the contracts are closed, when they are recorded as realized futures gains (losses).</FONT></P>
<P style="text-align: left;">
<FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">53</FONT></P>
</DIV>

<DIV STYLE="page-break-before: always">&nbsp;</div>



<!--$$/page=-->
<A name="page_189"></A><BR>

<a name="_bclPageBorder189"></a><DIV STYLE="WIDTH: 100%; PADDING-RIGHT: 0%; PADDING-LEFT: 0%">
<P style="text-align: left;">
<FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">Mid-Cap Index Fund</FONT></P>
<P style="text-align: left;">
<FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">During the year ended December 31, 2014, the fund&#146;s average investments in long and short futures contracts represented less than 1% and 0% of net assets, respectively, based on the average of aggregate settlement values at each quarter-end during the period.</FONT></P>
<P style="text-align: left;">
<FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">3. Swap Contracts: The fund has entered into equity swap contracts to earn the total return on selected reference stocks in the fund&#146;s target index. Under the terms of the swaps, the fund receives the total return on the referenced stock (i.e., receiving the increase or paying the decrease in value of the selected reference stock and receiving the equivalent of any dividends in respect of the selected referenced stock) over a specified period of time, applied to a notional amount that represents the value of a designated number of shares of the selected reference stock at the beginning of the equity swap contract. The fund also pays a floating rate that is based on short-term interest rates, applied to the notional amount. At the same time, the fund invests an amount approximating the notional amount of the swap in high-quality temporary cash investments.</FONT></P>
<P style="text-align: left;">
<FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">The notional amounts of swap contracts are not recorded in the Statement of Net Assets. Swaps are valued daily based on market quotations received from independent pricing services or recognized dealers and the change in value is recorded in the Statement of Net Assets as an asset (liability) and in the Statement of Operations as unrealized appreciation (depreciation) until termination of the swap, at which time realized gain (loss) is recorded. A risk associated with all types of swaps is the possibility that a counterparty may default on its obligation to pay net amounts due to the fund. The fund&#146;s maximum amount subject to counterparty risk is the unrealized appreciation on the swap contract. The fund mitigates its counterparty risk by entering into swaps only with a diverse group of pre-qualified counterparties, monitoring their financial strength, entering into master netting arrangements with its counterparties, and requiring its counterparties to transfer collateral as security for their performance. In the event of a counterparty&#146;s default (including bankruptcy), the fund may terminate any swap contracts with that counterparty, determine the net amount owed by either party in accordance with its master netting arrangements, and sell or retain any collateral held up to the net amount owed to the fund under the master netting arrangements. The swap contracts contain provisions whereby a counterparty may terminate open contracts if the fund net assets decline below a certain level, triggering a payment by the fund if the fund is in a net liability position at the time of the termination. The payment amount would be reduced by any collateral the fund has pledged. Any securities pledged as collateral for open contracts are noted in the Statement of Net Assets. The value of collateral received or pledged is compared daily to the value of the swap contracts exposure with each counterparty, and any difference, if in excess of a specified minimum transfer amount, is adjusted and settled within two business days.</FONT></P>
<P style="text-align: left;">
<FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">During the year ended December 31, 2014, the fund&#146;s average amounts of total return swaps represented less than 1% of net assets, based on the average of notional amounts at each quarter-end during the period. The fund had no open swap contracts at December 31, 2014.</FONT></P>
<P style="text-align: left;">
<FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">4. Federal Income Taxes: The fund intends to continue to qualify as a regulated investment company and distribute all of its taxable income. Management has analyzed the fund&#146;s tax positions taken for all open federal income tax years (December 31, 2011&#150;2014), and has concluded that no provision for federal income tax is required in the fund&#146;s financial statements.</FONT></P>
<P style="text-align: left;">
<FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">5. Distributions: Distributions to shareholders are recorded on the ex-dividend date.</FONT></P>
<P style="text-align: left;">
<FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">54</FONT></P>

<A name="page_190"></A><BR>

<a name="_bclPageBorder190"></a><DIV STYLE="WIDTH: 100%; PADDING-RIGHT: 0%; PADDING-LEFT: 0%">
<P style="text-align: left;">
<FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">Mid-Cap Index Fund</FONT></P>
<P style="text-align: left;">
<FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">6. Securities Lending: To earn additional income, the fund lends its securities to qualified institutional borrowers. Security loans are required to be secured at all times by collateral in an amount at least equal to the market value of securities loaned. Daily market fluctuations could cause the value of loaned securities to be more or less than the value of the collateral received. When this occurs, the collateral is adjusted and settled on the next business day. The fund further mitigates its counterparty risk by entering into securities lending transactions only with a diverse group of prequalified counterparties, monitoring their financial strength, and entering into master securities lending agreements with its counterparties. The master securities lending agreements provide that, in the event of a counterparty&#146;s default (including bankruptcy), the fund may terminate any loans with that borrower, determine the net amount owed, and sell or retain the collateral up to the net amount owed to the fund; however, such actions may be subject to legal proceedings. While collateral mitigates counterparty risk, in the absence of a default the fund may experience delays and costs in recovering the securities loaned. The fund invests cash collateral received in Vanguard Market Liquidity Fund, and records a liability in the Statement of Net Assets for the return of the collateral, during the period the securities are on loan. Securities lending income represents fees charged to borrowers plus income earned on invested cash collateral, less expenses associated with the loan.</FONT></P>
<P style="text-align: left;">
<FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">7</FONT><FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">. Credit Facility: The fund and certain other funds managed by The Vanguard Group participate in a &#36;2.</FONT><FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">8</FONT><FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">9 billion committed credit facility provided by a syndicate of lenders pursuant to a credit agreement that may be renewed annually; each fund is individually liable for its borrowings, if any, under the credit facility. Borrowings may be utilized for temporary and emergency purposes, and are subject to the fund&#146;s regulatory and contractual borrowing restrictions. The participating funds are charged administrative fees and an annual commitment fee of 0.06% of the undrawn amount of the facility; these fees are allocated to the funds based on a method approved by the fund&#146;s board of trustees and included in Management and Administrative expenses on the fund&#146;s Statement of Operations. Any borrowings under this facility bear interest at a rate equal to the higher of the federal funds rate or LIBOR reference rate plus an agreed-upon spread.</FONT></P>
<P style="text-align: left;">
<FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">The fund had no borrowings outstanding at December 31, 2014, or at any time during the period then ended.</FONT></P>
<P style="text-align: left;">
<FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">8</FONT><FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">. Other: Dividend income is recorded on the ex-dividend date. Interest income includes income distributions received from Vanguard Market Liquidity Fund and is accrued daily. Premiums and discounts on debt securities purchased are amortized and accreted, respectively, to interest income over the lives of the respective securities. Security transactions are accounted for on the date securities are bought or sold. Costs used to determine realized gains (losses) on the sale of investment securities are those of the specific securities sold.</FONT></P>
<P style="text-align: left;">
<FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">Each class of shares has equal rights as to assets and earnings, except that each class separately bears certain class-specific expenses related to maintenance of shareholder accounts (included in Management and Administrative expenses) and shareholder reporting. Marketing and distribution expenses are allocated to each class of shares based on a method approved by the board of trustees. Income, other non-class-specific expenses, and gains and losses on investments are allocated to each class of shares based on its relative net assets.</FONT></P>
<P style="text-align: left;">

The fund&#146;s trustees and officers are also directors and officers of Vanguard.</FONT></P>
<P style="text-align: left;">
<FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">C. </FONT><FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">Various inputs may be used to determine the value of the fund&#146;s investments. These inputs are summarized in three broad levels for financial statement purposes. The inputs or methodologies used to value securities are not necessarily an indication of the risk associated with investing in those securities.</FONT></P>

<FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">Level 2</FONT><FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">&#151;Other significant observable inputs (including quoted prices for similar securities, interest rates, prepayment speeds, credit risk, etc.).</FONT></P>

<P style="text-align: left;">
<FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">Mid-Cap Index Fund</FONT></P>
<P style="text-align: left;">
<FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">E. </FONT><FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">Distributions are determined on a tax basis and may differ from net investment income and realized capital gains for financial reporting purposes. Differences may be permanent or temporary. Permanent differences are reclassified among capital accounts in the financial statements to reflect their tax character. Temporary differences arise when certain items of income, expense, gain, or loss are recognized in different periods for financial statement and tax purposes. These differences will reverse at some time in the future. Differences in classification may also result from the treatment of short-term gains as ordinary income for tax purposes.</FONT></P>
<P style="text-align: left;">
<FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">During the year ended December 31, 2014, the fund realized &#36;2,33</FONT><FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">7</FONT><FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">,</FONT><FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">88</FONT><FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">3,000 of net capital gains resulting from in-kind redemptions&#151;in which shareholders exchanged fund shares for securities held by the fund rather than for cash. Because such gains are not taxable to the fund, and are not distributed to shareholders, they have been reclassified from accumulated net realized losses to paid-in capital.</FONT></P>
<P style="text-align: left;">
<FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">Realized and unrealized gains (losses) on certain of the fund&#146;s swap contracts are treated as ordinary income (loss) for tax purposes. Realized losses of &#36;1,395,000 on swap contracts have been reclassified from accumulated net realized losses to overdistributed net investment income.</FONT></P>
<P style="text-align: left;">
<FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">For tax purposes, at December 31, 2014, the fund had &#36;12,6</FONT><FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">7</FONT><FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">6,000 of ordinary income available for distribution. The fund used capital loss carryforwards of &#36;</FONT><FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">7</FONT><FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">9,440,000 to offset taxable capital gains realized during the year ended December 31, 2014. At December 31, 2014, the fund had available capital losses totaling &#36;669,3</FONT><FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">87</FONT><FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">,000 to offset future net capital gains. Of this amount, &#36;294,96</FONT><FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">8</FONT><FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">,000 is subject to expiration on December 31, 201</FONT><FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">8</FONT><FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">. Capital losses of &#36;3</FONT><FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">7</FONT><FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">4,419,000 realized beginning in fiscal 2011 may be carried forward indefinitely under the Regulated Investment Company Modernization Act of 2010, but must be used before any expiring capital loss carryforwards.</FONT></P>
<P style="text-align: left;">
<FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">At December 31, 2014, the cost of investment securities for tax purposes was &#36;42,</FONT><FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">87</FONT><FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">2,699,000. <A name="page_207"></A><BR>

<a name="_bclPageBorder207"></a><DIV STYLE="WIDTH: 100%; PADDING-RIGHT: 0%; PADDING-LEFT: 0%">
<P style="text-align: left;">
<FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">Mid-Cap Growth Index Fund</FONT></P>
<P style="text-align: left;">
<FONT size=3 face="UniversLTStd,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">Notes to Financial Statements</FONT></P>
<P style="text-align: left;">
<FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">Vanguard Mid-Cap Growth Index Fund is registered under the Investment Company Act of 1940 as an open-end investment company, or mutual fund. The fund offers three classes of shares: Investor Shares, Admiral Shares, and ETF Shares. Investor Shares are available to any investor who meets the fund&#146;s minimum purchase requirements. Admiral Shares are designed for investors who meet certain administrative, service, and account-size criteria. ETF Shares are listed for trading on NYSE Arca; they can be purchased and sold through a broker.</FONT></P>
<P style="text-align: left;">
<FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">A. </FONT><FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">The following significant accounting policies conform to generally accepted accounting principles for U.S. investment companies. The fund consistently follows such policies in preparing its financial statements.</FONT></P>
<P style="text-align: left;">
<FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">1. Security Valuation: Securities are valued as of the close of trading on the New York Stock Exchange (generally 4 p.m., Eastern time) on the valuation date. Equity securities are valued at the latest quoted sales prices or official closing prices taken from the primary market in which each security trades; such securities not traded on the valuation date are valued at the mean of the latest quoted bid and asked prices. Securities for which market quotations are not readily available, or whose values have been materially affected by events occurring before the fund&#146;s pricing time but after the close of the securities&#146; primary markets, are valued by methods deemed by the board of trustees to represent fair value. Investments in Vanguard Market Liquidity Fund are valued at that fund&#146;s net asset value. Temporary cash investments acquired over 60 days to maturity are valued using the latest bid prices or using valuations based on a matrix system (which considers such factors as security prices, yields, maturities, and ratings), both as furnished by independent pricing services. Other temporary cash investments are valued at amortized cost, which approximates market value.</FONT></P>
<P style="text-align: left;">
<FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">2. Futures Contracts: The fund uses index futures contracts to a limited extent, with the objectives of maintaining full exposure to the stock market, enhancing returns, maintaining liquidity, and minimizing transaction costs. The fund may purchase futures contracts to immediately invest incoming cash in the market, or sell futures in response to cash outflows, thereby simulating a fully invested position in the underlying index while maintaining a cash balance for liquidity. The fund may seek to enhance returns by using futures contracts instead of the underlying securities when futures are believed to be priced more attractively than the underlying securities. The primary risks associated with the use of futures contracts are imperfect correlation between changes in market values of stocks held by the fund and the prices of futures contracts, and the possibility of an illiquid market. Counterparty risk involving futures is mitigated because a regulated clearinghouse is the counterparty instead of the clearing broker. To further mitigate counterparty risk, the fund trades futures contracts on an exchange, monitors the financial strength of its clearing brokers and clearinghouse, and has entered into clearing agreements with its clearing brokers. The clearinghouse imposes initial margin requirements to secure the fund&#146;s performance and requires daily settlement of variation margin representing changes in the market value of each contract.</FONT></P>
<P style="text-align: left;">
<FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">Futures contracts are valued at their quoted daily settlement prices. The aggregate settlement values of the contracts are not recorded in the Statement of Net Assets. Fluctuations in the value of the contracts are recorded in the Statement of Net Assets as an asset (liability) and in the Statement of Operations as unrealized appreciation (depreciation) until the contracts are closed, when they are recorded as realized futures gains (losses).</FONT></P>
<P style="text-align: left;">
<FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">During the year ended December 31, 2014, the fund&#146;s average investments in long and short futures contracts represented less than 1% and 0% of net assets, respectively, based on the average of aggregate settlement values at each quarter-end during the period.</FONT></P>
<P style="text-align: left;">
<FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">72</FONT></P>
</DIV>

<DIV STYLE="page-break-before: always">&nbsp;</div>



<!--$$/page=-->
<A name="page_208"></A><BR>

<a name="_bclPageBorder208"></a><DIV STYLE="WIDTH: 100%; PADDING-RIGHT: 0%; PADDING-LEFT: 0%">
<P style="text-align: left;">
<FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">Mid-Cap Growth Index Fund</FONT></P>
<P style="text-align: left;">
<FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">3. Federal Income Taxes: The fund intends to continue to qualify as a regulated investment company and distribute all of its taxable income. Management has analyzed the fund&#146;s tax positions taken for all open federal income tax years (December 31, 2011&#150;2014), and has concluded that no provision for federal income tax is required in the fund&#146;s financial statements.</FONT></P>
<P style="text-align: left;">
<FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">4. Distributions: Distributions to shareholders are recorded on the ex-dividend date.</FONT></P>
<P style="text-align: left;">
<FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">5. Securities Lending: To earn additional income, the fund lends its securities to qualified institutional borrowers. Security loans are required to be secured at all times by collateral in an amount at least equal to the market value of securities loaned. Daily market fluctuations could cause the value of loaned securities to be more or less than the value of the collateral received. When this occurs, the collateral is adjusted and settled on the next business day. The fund further mitigates its counterparty risk by entering into securities lending transactions only with a diverse group of prequalified counterparties, monitoring their financial strength, and entering into master securities lending agreements with its counterparties. The master securities lending agreements provide that, in the event of a counterparty&#146;s default (including bankruptcy), the fund may terminate any loans with that borrower, determine the net amount owed, and sell or retain the collateral up to the net amount owed to the fund; however, such actions may be subject to legal proceedings. While collateral mitigates counterparty risk, in the absence of a default the fund may experience delays and costs in recovering the securities loaned. The fund invests cash collateral received in Vanguard Market Liquidity Fund, and records a liability in the Statement of Net Assets for the return of the collateral, during the period the securities are on loan. Securities lending income represents fees charged to borrowers plus income earned on invested cash collateral, less expenses associated with the loan.</FONT></P>
<P style="text-align: left;">
<FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">6. Credit Facility: The fund and certain other funds managed by The Vanguard Group participate in a &#36;2.</FONT><FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">8</FONT><FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">9 billion committed credit facility provided by a syndicate of lenders pursuant to a credit agreement that may be renewed annually; each fund is individually liable for its borrowings, if any, under the credit facility. Borrowings may be utilized for temporary and emergency purposes, and are subject to the fund&#146;s regulatory and contractual borrowing restrictions. The participating funds are charged administrative fees and an annual commitment fee of 0.06% of the undrawn amount of the facility; these fees are allocated to the funds based on a method approved by the fund&#146;s board of trustees and included in Management and Administrative expenses on the fund&#146;s Statement of Operations. Any borrowings under this facility bear interest at a rate equal to the higher of the federal funds rate or LIBOR reference rate plus an agreed-upon spread.</FONT></P>
<P style="text-align: left;">
<FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">The fund had no borrowings outstanding at December 31, 2014, or at any time during the period then ended.</FONT></P>
<P style="text-align: left;">
<FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">7</FONT><FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">. Other: Dividend income is recorded on the ex-dividend date. Interest income includes income distributions received from Vanguard Market Liquidity Fund and is accrued daily. Premiums and discounts on debt securities purchased are amortized and accreted, respectively, to interest income over the lives of the respective securities. Security transactions are accounted for on the date securities are bought or sold. Costs used to determine realized gains (losses) on the sale of investment securities are those of the specific securities sold.</FONT></P>
<P style="text-align: left;">
<FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">Each class of shares has equal rights as to assets and earnings, except that each class separately bears certain class-specific expenses related to maintenance of shareholder accounts (included in Management and Administrative expenses) and shareholder reporting. Marketing and distribution expenses are allocated to each class of shares based on a method approved by the board of trustees. Income, other non-class-specific expenses, and gains and losses on investments are allocated to each class of shares based on its relative net assets.</FONT></P>

<A name="page_224"></A><BR>

<a name="_bclPageBorder224"></a><DIV STYLE="WIDTH: 100%; PADDING-RIGHT: 0%; PADDING-LEFT: 0%">
<P style="text-align: left;">
<FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">Mid-Cap Value Index Fund</FONT></P>
<P style="text-align: left;">
<FONT size=3 face="UniversLTStd,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">Notes to Financial Statements</FONT></P>
<P style="text-align: left;">
<FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">Vanguard Mid-Cap Value Index Fund is registered under the Investment Company Act of 1940 as an open-end investment company, or mutual fund. The fund offers three classes of shares: Investor Shares, Admiral Shares, and ETF Shares. Investor Shares are available to any investor who meets the fund&#146;s minimum purchase requirements. Admiral Shares are designed for investors who meet certain administrative, service, and account-size criteria. ETF Shares are listed for trading on NYSE Arca; they can be purchased and sold through a broker.</FONT></P>
<P style="text-align: left;">
<FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">A. </FONT><FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">The following significant accounting policies conform to generally accepted accounting principles for U.S. investment companies. The fund consistently follows such policies in preparing its financial statements.</FONT></P>
<P style="text-align: left;">
<FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">1. Security Valuation: Securities are valued as of the close of trading on the New York Stock Exchange (generally 4 p.m., Eastern time) on the valuation date. Equity securities are valued at the latest quoted sales prices or official closing prices taken from the primary market in which each security trades; such securities not traded on the valuation date are valued at the mean of the latest quoted bid and asked prices. Securities for which market quotations are not readily available, or whose values have been materially affected by events occurring before the fund&#146;s pricing time but after the close of the securities&#146; primary markets, are valued by methods deemed by the board of trustees to represent fair value. Investments in Vanguard Market Liquidity Fund are valued at that fund&#146;s net asset value. Temporary cash investments acquired over 60 days to maturity are valued using the latest bid prices or using valuations based on a matrix system (which considers such factors as security prices, yields, maturities, and ratings), both as furnished by independent pricing services. Other temporary cash investments are valued at amortized cost, which approximates market value.</FONT></P>
<P style="text-align: left;">
<FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">2. Futures Contracts: The fund uses index futures contracts to a limited extent, with the objectives of maintaining full exposure to the stock market, enhancing returns, maintaining liquidity, and minimizing transaction costs. The fund may purchase futures contracts to immediately invest incoming cash in the market, or sell futures in response to cash outflows, thereby simulating a fully invested position in the underlying index while maintaining a cash balance for liquidity. The fund may seek to enhance returns by using futures contracts instead of the underlying securities when futures are believed to be priced more attractively than the underlying securities. The primary risks associated with the use of futures contracts are imperfect correlation between changes in market values of stocks held by the fund and the prices of futures contracts, and the possibility of an illiquid market. Counterparty risk involving futures is mitigated because a regulated clearinghouse is the counterparty instead of the clearing broker. To further mitigate counterparty risk, the fund trades futures contracts on an exchange, monitors the financial strength of its clearing brokers and clearinghouse, and has entered into clearing agreements with its clearing brokers. The clearinghouse imposes initial margin requirements to secure the fund&#146;s performance and requires daily settlement of variation margin representing changes in the market value of each contract.</FONT></P>
<P style="text-align: left;">
<FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">Futures contracts are valued at their quoted daily settlement prices. The aggregate settlement values of the contracts are not recorded in the Statement of Net Assets. Fluctuations in the value of the contracts are recorded in the Statement of Net Assets as an asset (liability) and in the Statement of Operations as unrealized appreciation (depreciation) until the contracts are closed, when they are recorded as realized futures gains (losses).</FONT></P>
<P style="text-align: left;">
<FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">89</FONT></P>
</DIV>

<DIV STYLE="page-break-before: always">&nbsp;</div>



<!--$$/page=-->
<A name="page_225"></A><BR>

<a name="_bclPageBorder225"></a><DIV STYLE="WIDTH: 100%; PADDING-RIGHT: 0%; PADDING-LEFT: 0%">
<P style="text-align: left;">
<FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">Mid-Cap Value Index Fund</FONT></P>
<P style="text-align: left;">
<FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">During the year ended December 31, 2014, the fund&#146;s average investments in long and short futures contracts represented less than 1% and 0% of net assets, respectively, based on the average of aggregate settlement values at each quarter-end during the period.</FONT></P>
<P style="text-align: left;">
<FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">3. Federal Income Taxes: The fund intends to continue to qualify as a regulated investment company and distribute all of its taxable income. Management has analyzed the fund&#146;s tax positions taken for all open federal income tax years (December 31, 2011&#150;2014), and has concluded that no provision for federal income tax is required in the fund&#146;s financial statements.</FONT></P>
<P style="text-align: left;">
<FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">4. Distributions: Distributions to shareholders are recorded on the ex-dividend date.</FONT></P>
<P style="text-align: left;">
<FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">5. Securities Lending: To earn additional income, the fund lends its securities to qualified institutional borrowers. Security loans are required to be secured at all times by collateral in an amount at least equal to the market value of securities loaned. Daily market fluctuations could cause the value of loaned securities to be more or less than the value of the collateral received. When this occurs, the collateral is adjusted and settled on the next business day. The fund further mitigates its counterparty risk by entering into securities lending transactions only with a diverse group of prequalified counterparties, monitoring their financial strength, and entering into master securities lending agreements with its counterparties. The master securities lending agreements provide that, in the event of a counterparty&#146;s default (including bankruptcy), the fund may terminate any loans with that borrower, determine the net amount owed, and sell or retain the collateral up to the net amount owed to the fund; however, such actions may be subject to legal proceedings. While collateral mitigates counterparty risk, in the absence of a default the fund may experience delays and costs in recovering the securities loaned. The fund invests cash collateral received in Vanguard Market Liquidity Fund, and records a liability in the Statement of Net Assets for the return of the collateral, during the period the securities are on loan. Securities lending income represents fees charged to borrowers plus income earned on invested cash collateral, less expenses associated with the loan.</FONT></P>
<P style="text-align: left;">
<FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">6. Credit Facility: The fund and certain other funds managed by The Vanguard Group participate in a &#36;2.</FONT><FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">8</FONT><FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">9 billion committed credit facility provided by a syndicate of lenders pursuant to a credit agreement that may be renewed annually; each fund is individually liable for its borrowings, if any, under the credit facility. Borrowings may be utilized for temporary and emergency purposes, and are subject to the fund&#146;s regulatory and contractual borrowing restrictions. The participating funds are charged administrative fees and an annual commitment fee of 0.06% of the undrawn amount of the facility; these fees are allocated to the funds based on a method approved by the fund&#146;s board of trustees and included in Management and Administrative expenses on the fund&#146;s Statement of Operations. Any borrowings under this facility bear interest at a rate equal to the higher of the federal funds rate or LIBOR reference rate plus an agreed-upon spread.</FONT></P>
<P style="text-align: left;">
<FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">The fund had no borrowings outstanding at December 31, 2014, or at any time during the period then ended.</FONT></P>
<P style="text-align: left;">
<FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">7</FONT><FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">. Other: Dividend income is recorded on the ex-dividend date. Interest income includes income distributions received from Vanguard Market Liquidity Fund and is accrued daily. Premiums and discounts on debt securities purchased are amortized and accreted, respectively, to interest income over the lives of the respective securities. Security transactions are accounted for on the date securities are bought or sold. Costs used to determine realized gains (losses) on the sale of investment securities are those of the specific securities sold.</FONT></P>

<FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">In our opinion, the accompanying statement of net assets&#151;investments summary and statements of net assets and the related statements of operations and of changes in net assets and the financial highlights present fairly, in all material respects, the financial position of Vanguard Extended Market Index Fund, Vanguard Mid-Cap Index Fund, Vanguard Mid-Cap Growth Index Fund and Vanguard Mid-Cap Value Index Fund (constituting separate portfolios of Vanguard Index Funds, hereafter referred to as the &#147;Funds&#148;) at December 31, 2014, the results of each of their operations for the year then ended, the changes in each of their net assets for each of the two years in the period then ended, and the financial highlights for each of the periods indicated, in conformity with accounting principles generally accepted in the United States of America. These financial statements and financial highlights (hereafter referred to as &#147;financial statements&#148;) are the responsibility of the Funds&#146; management. Our responsibility is to express an opinion on these financial statements based on our audits. We conducted our audits of these financial statements in accordance with the standards of the Public Company Accounting Oversight Board (United States). Those standards require that we plan and perform the audit to obtain reasonable assurance about whether the financial statements are free of material misstatement. An audit includes examining, on a test basis, evidence supporting the amounts and disclosures in the financial statements, assessing the accounting principles used and significant estimates made by management, and evaluating the overall financial statement presentation. We believe that our audits, which included confirmation of securities at December 31, 2014 by correspondence with the custodians and broker, by agreement to the underlying ownership records of the transfer agent and the application of alternative auditing procedures where securities purchased had not been received, provide a reasonable basis for our opinion.</FONT></P>

<P style="text-align: left;">
<FONT size=3 face="UniversLTStd,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">About Your Fund&#146;s Expenses</FONT></P>
<P style="text-align: left;">
<FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">As a shareholder of the fund, you incur ongoing costs, which include costs for portfolio management, administrative services, and shareholder reports (like this one), among others. Operating expenses, which are deducted from a fund&#146;s gross income, directly reduce the investment return of the fund.</FONT></P>
<P style="text-align: left;">
<FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">A fund&#146;s expenses are expressed as a percentage of its average net assets. This figure is known as the expense ratio. The following examples are intended to help you understand the ongoing costs (in dollars) of investing in your fund and to compare these costs with those of other mutual funds. The examples are based on an investment of &#36;1,000 made at the beginning of the period shown and held for the entire period.</FONT></P>
<P style="text-align: left;">
<FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">The accompanying table illustrates your fund&#146;s costs in two ways:</FONT></P>
<P style="text-align: left;">
<FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">&#149; </FONT><FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">Based on actual fund return. </FONT><FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">This section helps you to estimate the actual expenses that you paid over the period. The &#148;Ending Account Value&#147; shown is derived from the fund&#145;s actual return, and the third column shows the dollar amount that would have been paid by an investor who started with &#36;1,000 in the fund. You may use the information here, together with the amount you invested, to estimate the expenses that you paid over the period.</FONT></P>
<P style="text-align: left;">
<FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">To do so, simply divide your account value by &#36;1,000 (for example, an &#36;8,600 account value divided by &#36;1,000 = 8.6), then multiply the result by the number given for your fund under the heading &#148;Expenses Paid During Period.&#147;</FONT></P>
<P style="text-align: left;">
<FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">&#149; </FONT><FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">Based on hypothetical 5% yearly return. </FONT><FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">This section is intended to help you compare your fund&#145;s costs with those of other mutual funds. It assumes that the fund had a yearly return of 5% before expenses, but that the expense ratio is unchanged. In this case&#151;because the return used is not the fund&#146;s actual return&#151;the results do not apply to your investment. The example is useful in making comparisons because the Securities and Exchange Commission requires all mutual funds to calculate expenses based on a 5% return. You can assess your fund&#146;s costs by comparing this hypothetical example with the hypothetical examples that appear in shareholder reports of other funds.</FONT></P>
<P style="text-align: left;">
<FONT size=1 face="Univers-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">Note that the expenses shown in the table are meant to highlight and help you compare </FONT><I><FONT size=1 face="Univers-LightOblique,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">ongoing </FONT></I><FONT size=1 face="Univers-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">costs only and do not reflect transaction costs incurred by the fund for buying and selling securities. Further, the expenses do not include any purchase, redemption, or account service fees described in the fund prospectus. If such fees were applied to your account, your costs would be higher. Your fund does not carry a &#147;sales load.&#148;</FONT></P>
<P style="text-align: left;">
<FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">The calculations assume no shares were bought or sold during the period. Your actual costs may have been higher or lower, depending on the amount of your investment and the timing of any purchases or redemptions.</FONT></P>
<P style="text-align: left;">
<FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">You can find more information about the fund&#146;s expenses, including annual expense ratios, in the Financial Statements section of this report. For additional information on operating expenses and other shareholder costs, please refer to your fund&#146;s current prospectus.</FONT></P>

The dollar amounts shown as &#147;Expenses Paid&#148; are equal to the annualized expense ratio multiplied by the average account value over the period, multiplied by the number of days in the most recent six-month period, then divided by the number of days in the most recent 12-month period.</FONT></P>
