<DIV STYLE="page-break-before: always">&nbsp;</div>



<!--$$/page=-->
<A name="page_236"></A><BR>

<a name="_bclPageBorder236"></a><DIV STYLE="WIDTH: 100%; PADDING-RIGHT: 0%; PADDING-LEFT: 0%">
<P style="text-align: left;">
<FONT size=3 face="UniversLTStd,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">Glossary</FONT></P>
<P style="text-align: left;">
<FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">30-Day SEC Yield. </FONT><FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">A fund&#146;s 30-day SEC yield is derived using a formula specified by the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission. Under the formula, data related to the fund&#146;s security holdings in the previous 30 days are used to calculate the fund&#146;s hypothetical net income for that period, which is then annualized and divided by the fund&#146;s estimated average net assets over the calculation period. For the purposes of this calculation, a security&#146;s income is based on its current market yield to maturity (for bonds), its actual income (for asset-backed securities), or its projected dividend yield (for stocks). Because the SEC yield represents hypothetical annualized income, it will differ&#151;at times significantly&#151;from the fund&#146;s actual experience. As a result, the fund&#146;s income distributions may be higher or lower than implied by the SEC yield.</FONT></P>
<P style="text-align: left;">
<FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">Beta. </FONT><FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">A measure of the magnitude of a fund&#146;s past share-price fluctuations in relation to the ups and downs of a given market index. The index is assigned a beta of 1.00. Compared with a given index, a fund with a beta of 1.20 typically would have seen its share price rise or fall by 12% when the index rose or fell by 10%. For this report, beta is based on returns over the past 36 months for both the fund and the index. Note that a fund&#146;s beta should be reviewed in conjunction with its R-squared (see definition). The lower the R-squared, the less correlation there is between the fund and the index, and the less reliable beta is as an indicator of volatility.</FONT></P>
<P style="text-align: left;">
<FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">Dividend Yield. </FONT><FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">Dividend income earned by stocks, expressed as a percentage of the aggregate market value (or of net asset value, for a fund). The yield is determined by dividing the amount of the annual dividends by the aggregate value (or net asset value) at the end of the period. For a fund, the dividend yield is based solely on stock holdings and does not include any income produced by other investments.</FONT></P>
<P style="text-align: left;">
<FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">Earnings Growth Rate. </FONT><FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">The average annual rate of growth in earnings over the past five years for the stocks now in a fund.</FONT></P>
<P style="text-align: left;">
<FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">Equity Exposure. </FONT><FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">A measure that reflects a fund&#146;s investments in stocks and stock futures. Any holdings in short-term reserves are excluded.</FONT></P>
<P style="text-align: left;">
<FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">Expense Ratio. </FONT><FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">A fund&#146;s total annual operating expenses expressed as a percentage of the fund&#146;s average net assets. The expense ratio includes management and administrative expenses, but does not include the transaction costs of buying and selling portfolio securities.</FONT></P>
<P style="text-align: left;">
<FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">Foreign Holdings. </FONT><FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">The percentage of a fund represented by securities or depositary receipts of companies based outside the United States.</FONT></P>
<P style="text-align: left;">
<FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">Inception Date. </FONT><FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">The date on which the assets of a fund (or one of its share classes) are first invested in accordance with the fund&#146;s investment objective. For funds with a subscription period, the inception date is the day after that period ends. Investment performance is measured from the inception date.</FONT></P>
<P style="text-align: left;">
<FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">Median Market Cap. </FONT><FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">An indicator of the size of companies in which a fund invests; the midpoint of market capitalization (market price x shares outstanding) of a fund&#146;s stocks, weighted by the proportion of the fund&#146;s assets invested in each stock. Stocks representing half of the fund&#146;s assets have market capitalizations above the median, and the rest are below it.</FONT></P>
<P style="text-align: left;">
<FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">Price/Book Ratio. </FONT><FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">The share price of a stock divided by its net worth, or book value, per share. For a fund, the weighted average price/book ratio of the stocks it holds.</FONT></P>
<P style="text-align: left;">
<FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">101</FONT></P>
</DIV>

<DIV STYLE="page-break-before: always">&nbsp;</div>



<!--$$/page=-->
<A name="page_237"></A><BR>

<a name="_bclPageBorder237"></a><DIV STYLE="WIDTH: 100%; PADDING-RIGHT: 0%; PADDING-LEFT: 0%">
<P style="text-align: left;">
<FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">Price/Earnings Ratio. </FONT><FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">The ratio of a stock&#146;s current price to its per-share earnings over the past year. For a fund, the weighted average P/E of the stocks it holds. P/E is an indicator of market expectations about corporate prospects; the higher the P/E, the greater the expectations for a company&#146;s future growth.</FONT></P>
<P style="text-align: left;">
<FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">R-Squared. </FONT><FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">A measure of how much of a fund&#146;s past returns can be explained by the returns from the market in general, as measured by a given index. If a fund&#146;s total returns were precisely synchronized with an index&#146;s returns, its R-squared would be 1.00. If the fund&#146;s returns bore no relationship to the index&#146;s returns, its R-squared would be 0. For this report, R-squared is based on returns over the past 36 months for both the fund and the index.</FONT></P>
<P style="text-align: left;">
<FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">Return on Equity. </FONT><FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">The annual average rate of return generated by a company during the past five years for each dollar of shareholder&#146;s equity (net income divided by shareholder&#146;s equity). For a fund, the weighted average return on equity for the companies whose stocks it holds.</FONT></P>
<P style="text-align: left;">
<FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">Short-Term Reserves. </FONT><FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">The percentage of a fund invested in highly liquid, short-term securities that can be readily converted to cash.</FONT></P>
<P style="text-align: left;">
<FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">Turnover Rate. </FONT><FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">An indication of the fund&#146;s trading activity. Funds with high turnover rates incur higher transaction costs and may be more likely to distribute capital gains (which may be taxable to investors). The turnover rate excludes in-kind transactions, which have minimal impact on costs.</FONT></P>
<P style="text-align: left;">
<FONT size=2 face="UniversLTStd,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">Benchmark Information</FONT></P>
<P style="text-align: left;">
<FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">Spliced Extended Market Index: </FONT><FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">Dow Jones Wilshire 4500 Index through June 17, 2005; S&amp;P Transitional Completion Index through September 16, 2005; S&amp;P Completion Index thereafter.</FONT></P>
<P style="text-align: left;">
<FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">Spliced Mid-Cap Growth Index: </FONT><FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">MSCI US Mid Cap Growth Index through April 16, 2013; CRSP US Mid Cap Growth Index thereafter.</FONT></P>
<P style="text-align: left;">
<FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">Spliced Mid-Cap Index: </FONT><FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">S&amp;P MidCap 400 Index through May 16, 2003;&#160;MSCI US Mid Cap 450 Index through January 30, 2013;&#160;CRSP US Mid Cap Index thereafter.</FONT></P>
<P style="text-align: left;">
<FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">Spliced Mid-Cap Value Index: </FONT><FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">MSCI US Mid Cap Value Index through April 16, 2013; CRSP US Mid Cap Value Index thereafter.</FONT></P>
<P style="text-align: left;">
<FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">102</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=3 face=UniversLTStd,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif><STRONG>The People Who Govern Your Fund</STRONG></FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>The trustees of your mutual fund are there to see that the fund is operated and managed in your best interests since, as a shareholder, you are a part owner of the fund. Your fund&#8217;s trustees also serve on the board of directors of The Vanguard Group, Inc., which is owned by the Vanguard funds and provides services to them on an at-cost basis.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>A majority of Vanguard&#8217;s board members are independent, meaning that they have no affiliation with Vanguard or the funds they oversee, apart from the sizable personal investments they have made as private individuals. The independent board members have distinguished backgrounds in business, academia, and public service. Each of the trustees and executive officers oversees 1</FONT><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>77 </FONT><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>Vanguard funds.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>The following table provides information for each trustee and executive officer of the fund. More information about the trustees is in the </FONT><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-LightObl,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>Statement of Additional Information</FONT><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>, which can be obtained, without charge, by contacting Vanguard at </FONT><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>8</FONT><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>00-662-</FONT><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>7</FONT><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>44</FONT><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>7</FONT><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>, or online at vanguard.com.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=2 face=Univers,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif><STRONG>The mission continues</STRONG></FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=2 face=Univers-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>On May 1, 1975, Vanguard began operations, a fledgling company based on the simple but revolutionary idea that a mutual fund company should be managed solely in the interest of its investors.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=2 face=Univers-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>Four decades later, that revolutionary spirit continues to animate the enterprise. Vanguard remains on a mission to give investors the best chance of investment success.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=2 face=Univers-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>As we mark our 40th anniversary, we thank you for entrusting your assets to Vanguard and giving us the opportunity to help you reach your financial goals in the decades to come.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=3 face=UniversLTStd,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif><STRONG>Chairman&#8217;s Letter</STRONG></FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=2 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>Dear Shareholder,</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=2 face=UniversLTStd,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>U.S. stocks trumped their international counterparts in 2014 thanks to better-than-expected domestic economic growth, low interest rates and inflation, and strong corporate profits. Large companies were among the biggest beneficiaries of the stock market&#8217;s advance.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=2 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>For the 12 months ended December 31, 2014, Vanguard&#8217;s three large-capitalization U.S. index funds produced double-digit results for the third consecutive year. Vanguard Growth Index Fund returned 13.47% and Vanguard Value Index Fund returned 13.05%. Vanguard Large-Cap Index Fund, which holds both growth and value stocks, returned 13.24%. (All returns are for the funds&#8217; Investor Shares.)</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=2 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>All three funds closely tracked their target indexes and surpassed the average return of their peers.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=2 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>Please note that your fund&#8217;s Signal</FONT><SUP><FONT size=2 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>&#174; </FONT></SUP><FONT size=2 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>Shares were converted to Admiral Shares in October 2014 as part of a year-long plan to phase out Signal Shares and streamline Vanguard&#8217;s offerings.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=2 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>If you hold any of these funds in a taxable account, you may wish to review the table of after-tax returns that appears later in this report.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=2 face=UniversLTStd,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif><STRONG>U.S. stocks finished strongly for the sixth straight year</STRONG></FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=2 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>U.S. stocks returned nearly 13% for the 12 months, posting gains for the sixth consecutive calendar year.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=2 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>Although the Federal Reserve ended its bond-buying program in October, its stance that it would be &#8220;patient&#8221; in deciding when to increase short-term interest rates seemed to reassure investors. Other central banks&#8212;including the Bank of Japan, the European Central Bank, and the People&#8217;s Bank of China&#8212;announced significant stimulus measures.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=2 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>International stocks didn&#8217;t fare as well as those in the United States, returning about &#8211;3% in dollar terms. Their performance suffered as many foreign currencies weakened against the U.S. dollar. Emerging-market stocks rose slightly, and stocks from the developed markets of Europe and the Pacific region retreated.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=2 face=UniversLTStd,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif><STRONG>Defying analysts&#8217; expectations, bond prices rose during the period</STRONG></FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=2 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>Bond prices received a boost from moves by many of the world&#8217;s central banks, along with global economic, market, and geopolitical challenges that drew</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>5</FONT></P></DIV>

<DIV style="PADDING-LEFT: 0%; PADDING-RIGHT: 0%">

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=2 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>investors to perceived safe havens. In an unexpected rebound from last year, the broad U.S. bond market returned 5.97%.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=2 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>Even though the Fed pared back its bond purchases, prices climbed and yields fell. (Bond prices and yields move in opposite directions.) The yield of the 10-year Treasury note ended December at 2.19%, down from 2.97% at the close of December 2013.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=2 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>Municipal bonds returned 9.05%, benefiting from increased demand and generally limited supply.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=2 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>International bond markets (as measured by the Barclays Global Aggregate Index ex USD) returned &#8211;3.08%.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=2 face=UniversLTStd,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif><STRONG>Investors in 2014 favored large-caps over small-caps</STRONG></FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=2 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>In contrast to a year ago, large-cap stocks handsomely outpaced their small-cap brethren during the 12 months. Many investors were concerned about the &#8220;frothy&#8221; valuations of some small-cap stocks. They were less willing to invest in small companies, which have the potential for faster growth and higher returns than larger firms but also tend to be riskier and more volatile.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=2 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>In this environment, Vanguard&#8217;s three large-cap index funds posted strong returns in most market segments. As was the case six months ago, growth</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=2 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>stocks performed slightly better than value, but the gap was much narrower than it was among smaller-caps.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=2 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>Each of the large-cap funds delivered positive returns for nine of the ten industry sectors. Stocks of technology, health care, and financial companies contributed most to their overall performance. Energy-related holdings detracted.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=2 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>Hurt by tumbling oil prices, the oil and gas sector recorded a negative result for all three funds. Still, the strong showings of </FONT><FONT size=2 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>the other sectors outweighed the weakness among oil and gas producers, service providers, and distributors.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=2 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>The Growth Index Fund&#8217;s performance was buoyed by its outsized technology holdings. It benefited from increased corporate spending on technology and a surge in mobile device sales. Health care turned in impressive returns as well, as new product development, mergers and acquisitions, and strategic alliances boosted pharmaceutical and biotechnology companies.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=2 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>The financial sector also helped drive the fund&#8217;s success. Real estate investment trusts (REITs) thrived amid low interest rates and the expanding economy, as did banks, insurers, and other financial services firms.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=2 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>The Large-Cap Index Fund&#8217;s performance mirrored that of the Growth Index Fund. Stocks in technology, health care, and financials added most to returns. Increased consumer spending gave a lift to the economy, and in particular to the consumer services and consumer goods sectors. Utilities, a small component of both the </FONT><FONT size=2 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>index and the fund, was a stalwart as severe winter weather boosted earnings and as low interest rates sent investors searching for higher yields.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=2 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>The Value Index Fund&#8217;s heavy allocation to financial stocks was a bright spot. Health care and technology also helped significantly.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=2 face=UniversLTStd,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif><STRONG>The funds all notched solid gains and met their ten-year objectives</STRONG></FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=2 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>For the decade ended December 31, 2014, the three large-cap index funds recorded average annual returns ranging from 8.50%</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=2 face=UniversLTStd,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif><STRONG>Vanguard&#8217;s outlook for investors: Expect less and stay balanced</STRONG></FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=2 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>In Vanguard&#8217;s recently published market outlook, global chief economist Joe Davis and his team discuss expected returns for various asset classes over the coming years. Although not bearish, our outlook on global stocks and bonds is the most guarded since 2006. The report cautions that, over the next decade, returns for a balanced portfolio are likely to be moderately below long-run historical averages.</FONT></P><FONT size=2>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>Our simulations indicate that the average annualized returns of a 60% equity/40% bond portfolio for the decade ending 2024 are most likely to be centered in the 3%&#8211;5% range after inflation, below the actual average after-inflation return of 5.6% for the same portfolio since 1926.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>Even so, Vanguard firmly believes that the principles for investing success&#8212;focusing on clear goals, a suitable asset allocation, low costs, and long-term discipline&#8212;remain unchanged.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>For more information about our expectations and the probability of various outcomes, see </FONT><FONT face=UniversLTStd-LightObl,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>Vanguard&#8217;s Economic and Investment Outlook</FONT><FONT face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>, available at vanguard.com/research.</FONT></P></FONT>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Cn,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>IMPORTANT: The projections and other information generated by the Vanguard Capital Markets Model (VCMM) regarding the likelihood of various investment outcomes are hypothetical in nature, do not reflect actual investment results, and are not guarantees of future results. Distribution of return outcomes from VCMM, derived from 10,000 simulations for U.S. equity returns and fixed income returns. Simulations as of September 30, 2014. Results from the model may vary with each use and over time. For more information, please see page 9.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=2 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>for the Growth Index Fund to 7.17% for the Value Index Fund. The Large-Cap Index Fund, which completed its first full decade of performance last year, posted an average annual return of 7.87%.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=2 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>Over the past ten years, the funds have met their primary objective of closely tracking their target indexes. In addition, each fund&#8217;s average annual return has exceeded that of its peer group.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=2 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>The funds&#8217; success in staying close to their target indexes reflects the skill of the advisor, the Vanguard Equity Investment Group. The group relies on its proven </FONT><FONT size=2 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>portfolio management strategies to produce benchmark-tracking returns regardless of external market conditions. At the same time, the funds&#8217; low costs help you keep more of the market&#8217;s returns.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=2 face=UniversLTStd,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif><STRONG>To build for the long term, start with a solid foundation</STRONG></FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=2 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>As the leader of a major investment firm, I get asked a lot of questions on all kinds of topics, from the outlook for global markets to the best fund choices for an IRA. But a topic that almost never comes up&#8212;and one that I consider perhaps the most important&#8212;is setting investment goals.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Cn,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>IMPORTANT: The projections and other information generated by the Vanguard Capital Markets Model regarding the likelihood of various investment outcomes are hypothetical in nature, do not reflect actual investment results, and are not guarantees of future results. VCMM results will vary with each use and over time.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-LightCn,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>The VCMM projections are based on a statistical analysis of historical data. Future returns may behave differently from the historical patterns captured in the VCMM. More important, the VCMM may be underestimating extreme negative scenarios unobserved in the historical period on which the model estimation is based.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-LightCn,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>The Vanguard Capital Markets Model</FONT><SUP><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-LightCn,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>&#174; </FONT></SUP><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-LightCn,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>is a proprietary financial simulation tool developed and maintained by Vanguard&#8217;s primary investment research and advice teams. The model forecasts distributions of future returns for a wide array of broad asset classes. Those asset classes include U.S. and international equity markets, several maturities of the U.S. Treasury and corporate fixed income markets, international fixed income markets, U.S. money markets, commodities, and certain alternative investment strategies. The theoretical and empirical foundation for the Vanguard Capital Markets Model is that the returns of various asset classes reflect the compensation investors require for bearing different types of systematic risk (beta). At the core of the model are estimates of the dynamic statistical relationship between risk factors and asset returns, obtained from statistical analysis based on available monthly financial and economic data from as early as 1960. Using a system of estimated equations, the model then applies a Monte Carlo simulation method to project the estimated interrelationships among risk factors and asset classes as well as uncertainty and randomness over time. The model generates a large set of simulated outcomes for each asset class over several time horizons. Forecasts are obtained by computing measures of central tendency in these simulations. Results produced by the tool will vary with each use and over time.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>9</FONT></P></DIV>

<DIV style="PAGE-BREAK-BEFORE: always">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV style="PADDING-LEFT: 0%; PADDING-RIGHT: 0%">

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=2 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>At Vanguard, we believe that following four </FONT><FONT size=2 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>timeless, straightforward principles can </FONT><FONT size=2 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>help put you on the right track toward </FONT><FONT size=2 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>investment success:</FONT><BR><BR><FONT size=2 face=UniversLTStd,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>&#8226; Goals. </FONT><FONT size=2 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>Create clear, appropriate </FONT><FONT size=2 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>investment goals.</FONT><BR><BR><FONT size=2 face=UniversLTStd,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>&#8226; Balance. </FONT><FONT size=2 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>Develop a suitable asset </FONT><FONT size=2 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>allocation using broadly diversified funds.</FONT><BR><BR><FONT size=2 face=UniversLTStd,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>&#8226; Cost. </FONT><FONT size=2 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>Minimize cost.</FONT><BR><BR><FONT size=2 face=UniversLTStd,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>&#8226; Discipline. </FONT><FONT size=2 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>Maintain perspective and </FONT><FONT size=2 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>long-term discipline.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=2 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>All four principles are essential, and the order in which they&#8217;re listed is intentional. Every good investment plan begins with a clearly defined goal, which sets the foundation for building your portfolio. (You can read more about our principles in </FONT><FONT size=2 face=UniversLTStd-LightObl,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>Vanguard&#8217;s Principles for Investing Success, </FONT><FONT size=2 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>available at vanguard.com/research.)</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=2 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>Setting an investment goal doesn&#8217;t have to be complicated. It can be as simple as saving for retirement or for a child&#8217;s college education. Being realistic about your goals&#8212;and how to meet them&#8212;can help you stick with your investment plan even when times get tough.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=2 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>We&#8217;ve recently welcomed a new year, which for many means a new beginning. Now is a perfect time to revisit your investment plan and make any necessary adjustments to help you reach your long-term financial goals.</FONT></P>

<A name="page_273"></A><BR>

<a name="_bclPageBorder273"></a><DIV STYLE="WIDTH: 100%; PADDING-RIGHT: 0%; PADDING-LEFT: 0%">
<P style="text-align: left;">
<FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">Growth Index Fund</FONT></P>
<P style="text-align: left;">
<FONT size=3 face="UniversLTStd,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">Notes to Financial Statements</FONT></P>
<P style="text-align: left;">
<FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">Vanguard Growth Index Fund is registered under the Investment Company Act of 1940 as an open-end investment company, or mutual fund. The fund offers four classes of shares: Investor Shares, Admiral Shares, Institutional Shares, and ETF Shares. Investor Shares are available to any investor who meets the fund&#146;s minimum purchase requirements. Admiral Shares and Institutional Shares are designed for investors who meet certain administrative, service, and account-size criteria. ETF Shares are listed for trading on NYSE Arca; they can be purchased and sold through a broker. Prior to October 24, 2014, the fund offered Signal Shares. Effective at the close of business on October 24, 2014, the Signal Shares were converted to Admiral Shares.</FONT></P>
<P style="text-align: left;">
<FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">A. </FONT><FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">The following significant accounting policies conform to generally accepted accounting principles for U.S. investment companies. The fund consistently follows such policies in preparing its financial statements.</FONT></P>
<P style="text-align: left;">
<FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">1. Security Valuation: Securities are valued as of the close of trading on the New York Stock Exchange (generally 4 p.m., Eastern time) on the valuation date. Equity securities are valued at the latest quoted sales prices or official closing prices taken from the primary market in which each security trades; such securities not traded on the valuation date are valued at the mean of the latest quoted bid and asked prices. Securities for which market quotations are not readily available, or whose values have been materially affected by events occurring before the fund&#146;s pricing time but after the close of the securities&#146; primary markets, are valued by methods deemed by the board of trustees to represent fair value. Investments in Vanguard Market Liquidity Fund are valued at that fund&#146;s net asset value. Temporary cash investments acquired over 60 days to maturity are valued using the latest bid prices or using valuations based on a matrix system (which considers such factors as security prices, yields, maturities, and ratings), both as furnished by independent pricing services. Other temporary cash investments are valued at amortized cost, which approximates market value.</FONT></P>
<P style="text-align: left;">
<FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">2. Futures Contracts: The fund uses index futures contracts to a limited extent, with the objectives of maintaining full exposure to the stock market, enhancing returns, maintaining liquidity, and minimizing transaction costs. The fund may purchase futures contracts to immediately invest incoming cash in the market, or sell futures in response to cash outflows, thereby simulating a fully invested position in the underlying index while maintaining a cash balance for liquidity. The fund may seek to enhance returns by using futures contracts instead of the underlying securities when futures are believed to be priced more attractively than the underlying securities. The primary risks associated with the use of futures contracts are imperfect correlation between changes in market values of stocks held by the fund and the prices of futures contracts, and the possibility of an illiquid market. Counterparty risk involving futures is mitigated because a regulated clearinghouse is the counterparty instead of the clearing broker. To further mitigate counterparty risk, the fund trades futures contracts on an exchange, monitors the financial strength of its clearing brokers and clearinghouse, and has entered into clearing agreements with its clearing brokers. The clearinghouse imposes initial margin requirements to secure the fund&#146;s performance and requires daily settlement of variation margin representing changes in the market value of each contract.</FONT></P>
<P style="text-align: left;">
<FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">Futures contracts are valued at their quoted daily settlement prices. The aggregate settlement values of the contracts are not recorded in the Statement of Net Assets. Fluctuations in the value of the contracts are recorded in the Statement of Net Assets as an asset (liability) and in the Statement of Operations as unrealized appreciation (depreciation) until the contracts are closed, when they are recorded as realized futures gains (losses).</FONT></P>
<P style="text-align: left;">
<FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">28</FONT></P>
</DIV>

<DIV STYLE="page-break-before: always">&nbsp;</div>



<!--$$/page=-->
<A name="page_274"></A><BR>

<a name="_bclPageBorder274"></a><DIV STYLE="WIDTH: 100%; PADDING-RIGHT: 0%; PADDING-LEFT: 0%">
<P style="text-align: left;">
<FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">Growth Index Fund</FONT></P>
<P style="text-align: left;">
<FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">During the year ended December 31, 2014, the fund&#146;s average investments in long and short futures contracts represented less than 1% and 0% of net assets, respectively, based on the average of aggregate settlement values at each quarter-end during the period.</FONT></P>
<P style="text-align: left;">
<FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">3. Federal Income Taxes: The fund intends to continue to qualify as a regulated investment company and distribute all of its taxable income. Management has analyzed the fund&#146;s tax positions taken for all open federal income tax years (December 31, 2011&#150;2014), and has concluded that no provision for federal income tax is required in the fund&#146;s financial statements.</FONT></P>
<P style="text-align: left;">
<FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">4. Distributions: Distributions to shareholders are recorded on the ex-dividend date.</FONT></P>
<P style="text-align: left;">
<FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">5. Securities Lending: To earn additional income, the fund lends its securities to qualified institutional borrowers. Security loans are required to be secured at all times by collateral in an amount at least equal to the market value of securities loaned. Daily market fluctuations could cause the value of loaned securities to be more or less than the value of the collateral received. When this occurs, the collateral is adjusted and settled on the next business day. The fund further mitigates its counterparty risk by entering into securities lending transactions only with a diverse group of prequalified counter-parties, monitoring their financial strength, and entering into master securities lending agreements with its counterparties. The master securities lending agreements provide that, in the event of a counterparty&#146;s default (including bankruptcy), the fund may terminate any loans with that borrower, determine the net amount owed, and sell or retain the collateral up to the net amount owed to the fund; however, such actions may be subject to legal proceedings. While collateral mitigates counterparty risk, in the absence of a default the fund may experience delays and costs in recovering the securities loaned. The fund invests cash collateral received in Vanguard Market Liquidity Fund, and records a liability in the Statement of Net Assets for the return of the collateral, during the period the securities are on loan. Securities lending income represents fees charged to borrowers plus income earned on invested cash collateral, less expenses associated with the loan.</FONT></P>
<P style="text-align: left;">
<FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">6. Credit Facility: The fund and certain other funds managed by The Vanguard Group participate in a &#36;2.</FONT><FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">8</FONT><FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">9 billion committed credit facility provided by a syndicate of lenders pursuant to a credit agreement that may be renewed annually; each fund is individually liable for its borrowings, if any, under the credit facility. Borrowings may be utilized for temporary and emergency purposes, and are subject to the fund&#146;s regulatory and contractual borrowing restrictions. The participating funds are charged administrative fees and an annual commitment fee of 0.06% of the undrawn amount of the facility; these fees are allocated to the funds based on a method approved by the fund&#146;s board of trustees and included in Management and Administrative expenses on the fund&#146;s Statement of Operations. Any borrowings under this facility bear interest at a rate equal to the higher of the federal funds rate or LIBOR reference rate plus an agreed-upon spread.</FONT></P>
<P style="text-align: left;">
<FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">The fund had no borrowings outstanding at December 31, 2014, or at any time during the period then ended.</FONT></P>
<P style="text-align: left;">
<FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">7</FONT><FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">. Other: Dividend income is recorded on the ex-dividend date. Interest income includes income distributions received from Vanguard Market Liquidity Fund and is accrued daily. Premiums and discounts on debt securities purchased are amortized and accreted, respectively, to interest income over the lives of the respective securities. Security transactions are accounted for on the date securities are bought or sold. Costs used to determine realized gains (losses) on the sale of investment securities are those of the specific securities sold.</FONT></P>
<P style="text-align: left;">
<FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">29</FONT></P>

<P style="text-align: left;">
<FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">Each class of shares has equal rights as to assets and earnings, except that each class separately bears certain class-specific expenses related to maintenance of shareholder accounts (included in Management and Administrative expenses) and shareholder reporting. Marketing and distribution expenses are allocated to each class of shares based on a method approved by the board of trustees. Income, other non-class-specific expenses, and gains and losses on investments are allocated to each class of shares based on its relative net assets.</FONT></P>
<P style="text-align: left;">
<FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">B. </FONT><FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">The Vanguard Group furnishes at cost investment advisory, corporate management, administrative, marketing, and distribution services. The costs of such services are allocated to the fund based on methods approved by the board of trustees. The fund has committed to invest up to 0.40% of its net assets in Vanguard. At December 31, 2014, the fund had contributed capital of &#36;4,304,000 to Vanguard (included in Other Assets), representing 0.01% of the fund&#146;s net assets and 1.</FONT><FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">7</FONT><FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">2% of Vanguard&#146;s capitalization. The fund&#146;s trustees and officers are also directors and officers of Vanguard.</FONT></P>
<P style="text-align: left;">
<FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">C. </FONT><FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">Various inputs may be used to determine the value of the fund&#146;s investments. These inputs are summarized in three broad levels for financial statement purposes. The inputs or methodologies used to value securities are not necessarily an indication of the risk associated with investing in those securities.</FONT></P>
<P style="text-align: left;">
<FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">Level 1</FONT><FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">&#151;Quoted prices in active markets for identical securities.</FONT></P>
<P style="text-align: left;">
<FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">Level 2</FONT><FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">&#151;Other significant observable inputs (including quoted prices for similar securities, interest rates, prepayment speeds, credit risk, etc.).</FONT></P>
<P style="text-align: left;">
<FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">Level 3</FONT><FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">&#151;Significant unobservable inputs (including the fund&#146;s own assumptions used to determine the fair value of investments).</FONT></P>

<P style="MARGIN:0px">&nbsp;</P>
<P style="text-align: left;">
<FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">Unrealized appreciation (depreciation) on open futures contracts is required to be treated as realized gain (loss) for tax purposes.</FONT></P>
<P style="text-align: left;">
<FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">E. </FONT><FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">Distributions are determined on a tax basis and may differ from net investment income and realized capital gains for financial reporting purposes. Differences may be permanent or temporary. Permanent differences are reclassified among capital accounts in the financial statements to reflect their tax character. Temporary differences arise when certain items of income, expense, gain, or loss are recognized in different periods for financial statement and tax purposes. These differences will reverse at some time in the future. Differences in classification may also result from the treatment of short-term gains as ordinary income for tax purposes.</FONT></P>
<P style="text-align: left;">
<FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">During the year ended December 31, 2014, the fund realized &#36;1,139,</FONT><FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">8</FONT><FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">46,000 of net capital gains resulting from in-kind redemptions&#151;in which shareholders exchanged fund shares for securities held by the fund rather than for cash. Because such gains are not taxable to the fund, and are not distributed to shareholders, they have been reclassified from accumulated net realized losses to paid-in capital.</FONT></P>
<P style="text-align: left;">
<FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">For tax purposes, at December 31, 2014, the fund had &#36;4,056,000 of ordinary income available for distribution. At December 31, 2014, the fund had available capital losses totaling &#36;409,</FONT><FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">7</FONT><FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">35,000 to offset future net capital gains. Of this amount, &#36;300,1</FONT><FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">77</FONT><FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">,000 is subject to expiration on December 31, 201</FONT><FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">7</FONT><FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">. Capital losses of &#36;109,55</FONT><FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">8</FONT><FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">,000 realized beginning in fiscal 2011 may be carried forward indefinitely under the Regulated Investment Company Modernization Act of 2010, but must be used before any expiring loss carryforwards.</FONT></P>
<P style="text-align: left;">
<FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">At December 31, 2014, the cost of investment securities for tax purposes was &#36;2</FONT><FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">8</FONT><FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">,046,263,000. Net unrealized appreciation of investment securities for tax purposes was &#36;1</FONT><FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">7</FONT><FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">,134,566,000, consisting of unrealized gains of &#36;1</FONT><FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">7</FONT><FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">,391,446,000 on securities that had risen in value since their purchase and &#36;256,</FONT><FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">88</FONT><FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">0,000 in unrealized losses on securities that had fallen in value since their purchase.</FONT></P>

<a name="_bclPageBorder294"></a><DIV STYLE="WIDTH: 100%; PADDING-RIGHT: 0%; PADDING-LEFT: 0%">
<P style="text-align: left;">
<FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">Value Index Fund</FONT></P>
<P style="text-align: left;">
<FONT size=3 face="UniversLTStd,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">Notes to Financial Statements</FONT></P>
<P style="text-align: left;">
<FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">Vanguard Value Index Fund is registered under the Investment Company Act of 1940 as an open-end investment company, or mutual fund. The fund offers four classes of shares: Investor Shares, Admiral Shares, Institutional Shares, and ETF Shares. Investor Shares are available to any investor who meets the fund&#146;s minimum purchase requirements. Admiral Shares and Institutional Shares are designed for investors who meet certain administrative, service, and account-size criteria. ETF Shares are listed for trading on NYSE Arca; they can be purchased and sold through a broker. Prior to October 24, 2014, the fund offered Signal Shares. Effective at the close of business on October 24, 2014, the Signal Shares were converted to Admiral Shares.</FONT></P>
<P style="text-align: left;">
<FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">A. </FONT><FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">The following significant accounting policies conform to generally accepted accounting principles for U.S. investment companies. The fund consistently follows such policies in preparing its financial statements.</FONT></P>
<P style="text-align: left;">
<FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">1. Security Valuation: Securities are valued as of the close of trading on the New York Stock Exchange (generally 4 p.m., Eastern time) on the valuation date. Equity securities are valued at the latest quoted sales prices or official closing prices taken from the primary market in which each security trades; such securities not traded on the valuation date are valued at the mean of the latest quoted bid and asked prices. Securities for which market quotations are not readily available, or whose values have been materially affected by events occurring before the fund&#146;s pricing time but after the close of the securities&#146; primary markets, are valued by methods deemed by the board of trustees to represent fair value. Investments in Vanguard Market Liquidity Fund are valued at that fund&#146;s net asset value. Temporary cash investments acquired over 60 days to maturity are valued using the latest bid prices or using valuations based on a matrix system (which considers such factors as security prices, yields, maturities, and ratings), both as furnished by independent pricing services. Other temporary cash investments are valued at amortized cost, which approximates market value.</FONT></P>
<P style="text-align: left;">
<FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">2. Futures Contracts: The fund uses index futures contracts to a limited extent, with the objectives of maintaining full exposure to the stock market, enhancing returns, maintaining liquidity, and minimizing transaction costs. The fund may purchase futures contracts to immediately invest incoming cash in the market, or sell futures in response to cash outflows, thereby simulating a fully invested position in the underlying index while maintaining a cash balance for liquidity. The fund may seek to enhance returns by using futures contracts instead of the underlying securities when futures are believed to be priced more attractively than the underlying securities. The primary risks associated with the use of futures contracts are imperfect correlation between changes in market values of stocks held by the fund and the prices of futures contracts, and the possibility of an illiquid market. Counterparty risk involving futures is mitigated because a regulated clearinghouse is the counterparty instead of the clearing broker. To further mitigate counterparty risk, the fund trades futures contracts on an exchange, monitors the financial strength of its clearing brokers and clearinghouse, and has entered into clearing agreements with its clearing brokers. The clearinghouse imposes initial margin requirements to secure the fund&#146;s performance and requires daily settlement of variation margin representing changes in the market value of each contract.</FONT></P>
<P style="text-align: left;">
<FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">Futures contracts are valued at their quoted daily settlement prices. The aggregate settlement values of the contracts are not recorded in the Statement of Net Assets. Fluctuations in the value of the contracts are recorded in the Statement of Net Assets as an asset (liability) and in the Statement of Operations as unrealized appreciation (depreciation) until the contracts are closed, when they are recorded as realized futures gains (losses).</FONT></P>
<P style="text-align: left;">
<FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">49</FONT></P>

<A name="page_295"></A><BR>

<a name="_bclPageBorder295"></a><DIV STYLE="WIDTH: 100%; PADDING-RIGHT: 0%; PADDING-LEFT: 0%">
<P style="text-align: left;">
<FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">Value Index Fund</FONT></P>
<P style="text-align: left;">
<FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">During the year ended December 31, 2014, the fund&#146;s average investments in long and short futures contracts represented less than 1% and 0% of net assets, respectively, based on the average of aggregate settlement values at each quarter-end during the period.</FONT></P>
<P style="text-align: left;">
<FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">3. Federal Income Taxes: The fund intends to continue to qualify as a regulated investment company and distribute all of its taxable income. Management has analyzed the fund&#146;s tax positions taken for all open federal income tax years (December 31, 2011&#150;2014), and has concluded that no provision for federal income tax is required in the fund&#146;s financial statements.</FONT></P>
<P style="text-align: left;">
<FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">4. Distributions: Distributions to shareholders are recorded on the ex-dividend date.</FONT></P>
<P style="text-align: left;">
<FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">5. Securities Lending: To earn additional income, the fund lends its securities to qualified institutional borrowers. Security loans are required to be secured at all times by collateral in an amount at least equal to the market value of securities loaned. Daily market fluctuations could cause the value of loaned securities to be more or less than the value of the collateral received. When this occurs, the collateral is adjusted and settled on the next business day. The fund further mitigates its counterparty risk by entering into securities lending transactions only with a diverse group of prequalified counter-parties, monitoring their financial strength, and entering into master securities lending agreements with its counterparties. The master securities lending agreements provide that, in the event of a counterparty&#146;s default (including bankruptcy), the fund may terminate any loans with that borrower, determine the net amount owed, and sell or retain the collateral up to the net amount owed to the fund; however, such actions may be subject to legal proceedings. While collateral mitigates counterparty risk, in the absence of a default the fund may experience delays and costs in recovering the securities loaned. The fund invests cash collateral received in Vanguard Market Liquidity Fund, and records a liability in the Statement of Net Assets for the return of the collateral, during the period the securities are on loan. Securities lending income represents fees charged to borrowers plus income earned on invested cash collateral, less expenses associated with the loan.</FONT></P>
<P style="text-align: left;">
<FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">6. Credit Facility: The fund and certain other funds managed by The Vanguard Group participate in a &#36;2.</FONT><FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">8</FONT><FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">9 billion committed credit facility provided by a syndicate of lenders pursuant to a credit agreement that may be renewed annually; each fund is individually liable for its borrowings, if any, under the credit facility. Borrowings may be utilized for temporary and emergency purposes, and are subject to the fund&#146;s regulatory and contractual borrowing restrictions. The participating funds are charged administrative fees and an annual commitment fee of 0.06% of the undrawn amount of the facility; these fees are allocated to the funds based on a method approved by the fund&#146;s board of trustees and included in Management and Administrative expenses on the fund&#146;s Statement of Operations. Any borrowings under this facility bear interest at a rate equal to the higher of the federal funds rate or LIBOR reference rate plus an agreed-upon spread.</FONT></P>
<P style="text-align: left;">
<FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">The fund had no borrowings outstanding at December 31, 2014, or at any time during the period then ended.</FONT></P>
<P style="text-align: left;">
<FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">7</FONT><FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">. Other: Dividend income is recorded on the ex-dividend date. Interest income includes income distributions received from Vanguard Market Liquidity Fund and is accrued daily. Premiums and discounts on debt securities purchased are amortized and accreted, respectively, to interest income over the lives of the respective securities. Security transactions are accounted for on the date securities are bought or sold. Costs used to determine realized gains (losses) on the sale of investment securities are those of the specific securities sold.</FONT></P>

<P style="text-align: left;">
<FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">Unrealized appreciation (depreciation) on open futures contracts is required to be treated as realized gain (loss) for tax purposes.</FONT></P>
<P style="text-align: left;">
<FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">E. </FONT><FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">Distributions are determined on a tax basis and may differ from net investment income and realized capital gains for financial reporting purposes. Differences may be permanent or temporary. Permanent differences are reclassified among capital accounts in the financial statements to reflect their tax character. Temporary differences arise when certain items of income, expense, gain, or loss are recognized in different periods for financial statement and tax purposes. These differences will reverse at some time in the future. Differences in classification may also result from the treatment of short-term gains as ordinary income for tax purposes.</FONT></P>
<P style="text-align: left;">
<FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">During the year ended December 31, 2014, the fund realized &#36;</FONT><FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">78</FONT><FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">4,</FONT><FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">8</FONT><FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">6</FONT><FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">7</FONT><FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">,000 of net capital gains resulting from in-kind redemptions&#151;in which shareholders exchanged fund shares for securities held by the fund rather than for cash. Because such gains are not taxable to the fund, and are not distributed to shareholders, they have been reclassified from accumulated net realized losses to paid-in capital.</FONT></P>
<P style="text-align: left;">
<FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">For tax purposes, at December 31, 2014, the fund had &#36;10,063,000 of ordinary income available for distribution. The fund used capital loss carryforwards of &#36;12,</FONT><FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">8</FONT><FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">35,000 to offset taxable capital gains realized during the year ended December 31, 2014. At December 31, 2014, the fund had available capital losses totaling &#36;356,42</FONT><FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">7</FONT><FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">,000 to offset future net capital gains. Of this amount, &#36;333,3</FONT><FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">77</FONT><FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">,000 is subject to expiration on December 31, 201</FONT><FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">7</FONT><FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">. Capital losses of &#36;23,050,000 realized beginning in fiscal 2011 may be carried forward indefinitely under the Regulated Investment Company Modernization Act of 2010, but must be used before any expiring loss carryforwards.</FONT></P>
<P style="text-align: left;">
<FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">At December 31, 2014, the cost of investment securities for tax purposes was &#36;2</FONT><FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">8</FONT><FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">,</FONT><FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">787</FONT><FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">,21</FONT><FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">8</FONT><FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">,000. Net unrealized appreciation of investment securities for tax purposes was &#36;</FONT><FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">7</FONT><FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">,664,0</FONT><FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">7</FONT><FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">1,000, consisting of unrealized gains of &#36;</FONT><FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">8</FONT><FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">,229,342,000 on securities that had risen in value since their purchase and &#36;565,2</FONT><FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">7</FONT><FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">1,000 in unrealized losses on securities that had fallen in value since their purchase.</FONT></P>
<P style="text-align: left;">
<FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">F. </FONT><FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">During the year ended December 31, 2014, the fund purchased &#36;</FONT><FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">8</FONT><FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">,333,501,000 of investment securities and sold &#36;3,</FONT><FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">7</FONT><FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">52,6</FONT><FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">7</FONT><FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">6,000 of investment securities, other than temporary cash investments. Purchases and sales include &#36;4,</FONT><FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">8</FONT><FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">2</FONT><FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">7</FONT><FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">,</FONT><FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">7</FONT><FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">53,000 and &#36;1,999,150,000, respectively, in connection with in-kind purchases and redemptions of the fund&#146;s capital shares.</FONT></P>

<A name="page_319"></A><BR>

<a name="_bclPageBorder319"></a><DIV STYLE="WIDTH: 100%; PADDING-RIGHT: 0%; PADDING-LEFT: 0%">
<P style="text-align: left;">
<FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">Large-Cap Index Fund</FONT></P>
<P style="text-align: left;">
<FONT size=3 face="UniversLTStd,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">Notes to Financial Statements</FONT></P>
<P style="text-align: left;">
<FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">Vanguard Large-Cap Index Fund is registered under the Investment Company Act of 1940 as an open-end investment company, or mutual fund. The fund offers four classes of shares: Investor Shares, Admiral Shares, Institutional Shares, and ETF Shares. Investor Shares are available to any investor who meets the fund&#146;s minimum purchase requirements. Admiral Shares and Institutional Shares are designed for investors who meet certain administrative, service, and account-size criteria. ETF Shares are listed for trading on NYSE Arca; they can be purchased and sold through a broker. Prior to October 24, 2014, the fund offered Signal Shares. Effective at the close of business on October 24, 2014, the Signal Shares were converted to Admiral Shares.</FONT></P>
<P style="text-align: left;">
<FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">A. </FONT><FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">The following significant accounting policies conform to generally accepted accounting principles for U.S. investment companies. The fund consistently follows such policies in preparing its financial statements.</FONT></P>
<P style="text-align: left;">
<FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">1. Security Valuation: Securities are valued as of the close of trading on the New York Stock Exchange (generally 4 p.m., Eastern time) on the valuation date. Equity securities are valued at the latest quoted sales prices or official closing prices taken from the primary market in which each security trades; such securities not traded on the valuation date are valued at the mean of the latest quoted bid and asked prices. Securities for which market quotations are not readily available, or whose values have been materially affected by events occurring before the fund&#146;s pricing time but after the close of the securities&#146; primary markets, are valued by methods deemed by the board of trustees to represent fair value. Investments in Vanguard Market Liquidity Fund are valued at that fund&#146;s net asset value. Temporary cash investments acquired over 60 days to maturity are valued using the latest bid prices or using valuations based on a matrix system (which considers such factors as security prices, yields, maturities, and ratings), both as furnished by independent pricing services. Other temporary cash investments are valued at amortized cost, which approximates market value.</FONT></P>
<P style="text-align: left;">
<FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">2. Futures Contracts: The fund uses index futures contracts to a limited extent, with the objectives of maintaining full exposure to the stock market, enhancing returns, maintaining liquidity, and minimizing transaction costs. The fund may purchase futures contracts to immediately invest incoming cash in the market, or sell futures in response to cash outflows, thereby simulating a fully invested position in the underlying index while maintaining a cash balance for liquidity. The fund may seek to enhance returns by using futures contracts instead of the underlying securities when futures are believed to be priced more attractively than the underlying securities. The primary risks associated with the use of futures contracts are imperfect correlation between changes in market values of stocks held by the fund and the prices of futures contracts, and the possibility of an illiquid market. Counterparty risk involving futures is mitigated because a regulated clearinghouse is the counterparty instead of the clearing broker. To further mitigate counterparty risk, the fund trades futures contracts on an exchange, monitors the financial strength of its clearing brokers and clearinghouse, and has entered into clearing agreements with its clearing brokers. The clearinghouse imposes initial margin requirements to secure the fund&#146;s performance and requires daily settlement of variation margin representing changes in the market value of each contract.</FONT></P>
<P style="text-align: left;">
<FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">Futures contracts are valued at their quoted daily settlement prices. The aggregate settlement values of the contracts are not recorded in the Statement of Net Assets. Fluctuations in the value of the contracts are recorded in the Statement of Net Assets as an asset (liability) and in the Statement of Operations as unrealized appreciation (depreciation) until the contracts are closed, when they are recorded as realized futures gains (losses).</FONT></P>
<P style="text-align: left;">
<FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">74</FONT></P>
</DIV>

<DIV STYLE="page-break-before: always">&nbsp;</div>



<!--$$/page=-->
<A name="page_320"></A><BR>

<a name="_bclPageBorder320"></a><DIV STYLE="WIDTH: 100%; PADDING-RIGHT: 0%; PADDING-LEFT: 0%">
<P style="text-align: left;">
<FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">Large-Cap Index Fund</FONT></P>
<P style="text-align: left;">
<FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">During the year ended December 31, 2014, the fund&#146;s average investments in long and short futures contracts represented less than 1% and 0% of net assets, respectively, based on the average of aggregate settlement values at each quarter-end during the period.</FONT></P>
<P style="text-align: left;">
<FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">3. Federal Income Taxes: The fund intends to continue to qualify as a regulated investment company and distribute all of its taxable income. Management has analyzed the fund&#146;s tax positions taken for all open federal income tax years (December 31, 2011&#150;2014), and has concluded that no provision for federal income tax is required in the fund&#146;s financial statements.</FONT></P>
<P style="text-align: left;">
<FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">4. Distributions: Distributions to shareholders are recorded on the ex-dividend date.</FONT></P>
<P style="text-align: left;">
<FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">5. Securities Lending: To earn additional income, the fund lends its securities to qualified institutional borrowers. Security loans are required to be secured at all times by collateral in an amount at least equal to the market value of securities loaned. Daily market fluctuations could cause the value of loaned securities to be more or less than the value of the collateral received. When this occurs, the collateral is adjusted and settled on the next business day. The fund further mitigates its counterparty risk by entering into securities lending transactions only with a diverse group of prequalified counter-parties, monitoring their financial strength, and entering into master securities lending agreements with its counterparties. The master securities lending agreements provide that, in the event of a counterparty&#146;s default (including bankruptcy), the fund may terminate any loans with that borrower, determine the net amount owed, and sell or retain the collateral up to the net amount owed to the fund; however, such actions may be subject to legal proceedings. While collateral mitigates counterparty risk, in the absence of a default the fund may experience delays and costs in recovering the securities loaned. The fund invests cash collateral received in Vanguard Market Liquidity Fund, and records a liability in the Statement of Net Assets for the return of the collateral, during the period the securities are on loan. Securities lending income represents fees charged to borrowers plus income earned on invested cash collateral, less expenses associated with the loan.</FONT></P>
<P style="text-align: left;">
<FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">6. Credit Facility: The fund and certain other funds managed by The Vanguard Group participate in a &#36;2.</FONT><FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">8</FONT><FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">9 billion committed credit facility provided by a syndicate of lenders pursuant to a credit agreement that may be renewed annually; each fund is individually liable for its borrowings, if any, under the credit facility. Borrowings may be utilized for temporary and emergency purposes, and are subject to the fund&#146;s regulatory and contractual borrowing restrictions. The participating funds are charged administrative fees and an annual commitment fee of 0.06% of the undrawn amount of the facility; these fees are allocated to the funds based on a method approved by the fund&#146;s board of trustees and included in Management and Administrative expenses on the fund&#146;s Statement of Operations. Any borrowings under this facility bear interest at a rate equal to the higher of the federal funds rate or LIBOR reference rate plus an agreed-upon spread.</FONT></P>
<P style="text-align: left;">
<FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">The fund had no borrowings outstanding at December 31, 2014, or at any time during the period then ended.</FONT></P>
<P style="text-align: left;">
<FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">7</FONT><FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">. Other: Dividend income is recorded on the ex-dividend date. Interest income includes income distributions received from Vanguard Market Liquidity Fund and is accrued daily. Premiums and discounts on debt securities purchased are amortized and accreted, respectively, to interest income over the lives of the respective securities. Security transactions are accounted for on the date securities are bought or sold. Costs used to determine realized gains (losses) on the sale of investment securities are those of the specific securities sold.</FONT></P>
<P style="text-align: left;">
<FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">75</FONT></P>

<FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">Large-Cap Index Fund</FONT></P>
<P style="text-align: left;">
<FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">Each class of shares has equal rights as to assets and earnings, except that each class separately bears certain class-specific expenses related to maintenance of shareholder accounts (included in Management and Administrative expenses) and shareholder reporting. Marketing and distribution expenses are allocated to each class of shares based on a method approved by the board of trustees. Income, other non-class-specific expenses, and gains and losses on investments are allocated to each class of shares based on its relative net assets.</FONT></P>
<P style="text-align: left;">
<FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">B. </FONT><FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">The Vanguard Group furnishes at cost investment advisory, corporate management, administrative, marketing, and distribution services. The costs of such services are allocated to the fund based on methods approved by the board of trustees. The fund has committed to invest up to 0.40% of its net assets in Vanguard. At December 31, 2014, the fund had contributed capital of &#36;944,000 to Vanguard (included in Other Assets), representing 0.01% of the fund&#146;s net assets and 0.3</FONT><FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">8</FONT><FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">% of Vanguard&#146;s capitalization. The fund&#146;s trustees and officers are also directors and officers of Vanguard.</FONT></P>
<P style="text-align: left;">
<FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">C. </FONT><FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">Various inputs may be used to determine the value of the fund&#146;s investments. These inputs are summarized in three broad levels for financial statement purposes. The inputs or methodologies used to value securities are not necessarily an indication of the risk associated with investing in those securities.</FONT></P>
<P style="text-align: left;">
<FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">Level 1</FONT><FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">&#151;Quoted prices in active markets for identical securities.</FONT></P>
<P style="text-align: left;">
<FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">Level 2</FONT><FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">&#151;Other significant observable inputs (including quoted prices for similar securities, interest rates, prepayment speeds, credit risk, etc.).</FONT></P>
<P style="text-align: left;">
<FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">Level 3</FONT><FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">&#151;Significant unobservable inputs (including the fund&#146;s own assumptions used to determine the fair value of investments).</FONT></P>
