<P style="MARGIN:0px">&nbsp;</P>
<P style="text-align: left;">
<FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">Unrealized appreciation (depreciation) on open futures contracts is required to be treated as realized gain (loss) for tax purposes.</FONT></P>
<P style="text-align: left;">
<FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">E. </FONT><FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">Distributions are determined on a tax basis and may differ from net investment income and realized capital gains for financial reporting purposes. Differences may be permanent or temporary. Permanent differences are reclassified among capital accounts in the financial statements to reflect their tax character. Temporary differences arise when certain items of income, expense, gain, or loss are recognized in different periods for financial statement and tax purposes. These differences will reverse at some time in the future. Differences in classification may also result from the treatment of short-term gains as ordinary income for tax purposes.</FONT></P>
<P style="text-align: left;">
<FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">During the year ended December 31, 2014, the fund realized &#36;</FONT><FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">7</FONT><FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">5,019,000 of net capital gains resulting from in-kind redemptions&#151;in which shareholders exchanged fund shares for securities held by the fund rather than for cash. Because such gains are not taxable to the fund, and are not distributed to shareholders, they have been reclassified from accumulated net realized losses to paid-in capital.</FONT></P>
<P style="text-align: left;">
<FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">For tax purposes, at December 31, 2014, the fund had &#36;1,3</FONT><FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">7</FONT><FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">3,000 of ordinary income available for distribution. The fund used capital loss carryforwards of &#36;14,</FONT><FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">7</FONT><FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">3</FONT><FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">7</FONT><FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">,000 to offset taxable capital gains realized during the year ended December 31, 2014. At December 31, 2014, the fund had available capital losses totaling &#36;36,01</FONT><FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">8</FONT><FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">,000 to offset future net capital gains. Of this amount, &#36;24,1</FONT><FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">77</FONT><FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">,000 is subject to expiration on December 31, 201</FONT><FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">8</FONT><FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">. Capital losses of &#36;11,</FONT><FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">8</FONT><FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">41,000 realized beginning in fiscal 2011 may be carried forward indefinitely under the Regulated Investment Company Modernization Act of 2010, but must be used before any expiring loss carryforwards.</FONT></P>
<P style="text-align: left;">
<FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">At December 31, 2014, the cost of investment securities for tax purposes was &#36;6,4</FONT><FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">7</FONT><FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">0,032,000. <P style="text-align: left;">
<FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">To the Board of Trustees of Vanguard Index Funds and the Shareholders of Vanguard Growth Index Fund, Vanguard Value Index Fund and Vanguard Large-Cap Index Fund:</FONT></P>
<P style="text-align: left;">
<FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">In our opinion, the accompanying statements of net assets and the related statements of operations and of changes in net assets and the financial highlights present fairly, in all material respects, the financial position of Vanguard Growth Index Fund, Vanguard Value Index Fund and Vanguard Large-Cap Index Fund (constituting separate portfolios of Vanguard Index Funds, hereafter referred to as the &#147;Funds&#148;) at December 31, 2014, the results of each of their operations for the year then ended, the changes in each of their net assets for each of the two years in the period then ended, and the financial highlights for each of the five years in the period then ended, in conformity with accounting principles generally accepted in the United States of America. These financial statements and financial highlights (hereafter referred to as &#147;financial statements&#148;) are the responsibility of the Funds&#146; management. Our responsibility is to express an opinion on these financial statements based on our audits. We conducted our audits of these financial statements in accordance with the standards of the Public Company Accounting Oversight Board (United States). Those standards require that we plan and perform the audit to obtain reasonable assurance about whether the financial statements are free of material misstatement. An audit includes examining, on a test basis, evidence supporting the amounts and disclosures in the financial statements, assessing the accounting principles used and significant estimates made by management, and evaluating the overall financial statement presentation. We believe that our audits, which included confirmation of securities at December 31, 2014 by correspondence with the custodians and brokers, by agreement to the underlying ownership records of the transfer agent and the application of alternative auditing procedures where securities purchased had not been received, provide a reasonable basis for our opinion.</FONT></P>

<P style="text-align: left;">
<FONT size=3 face="UniversLTStd,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">About Your Fund&#146;s Expenses</FONT></P>
<P style="text-align: left;">
<FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">As a shareholder of the fund, you incur ongoing costs, which include costs for portfolio management, administrative services, and shareholder reports (like this one), among others. Operating expenses, which are deducted from a fund&#146;s gross income, directly reduce the investment return of the fund.</FONT></P>
<P style="text-align: left;">
<FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">A fund&#146;s expenses are expressed as a percentage of its average net assets. This figure is known as the expense ratio. The following examples are intended to help you understand the ongoing costs (in dollars) of investing in your fund and to compare these costs with those of other mutual funds. The examples are based on an investment of &#36;1,000 made at the beginning of the period shown and held for the entire period.</FONT></P>
<P style="text-align: left;">
<FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">The accompanying table illustrates your fund&#146;s costs in two ways:</FONT></P>
<P style="text-align: left;">
<FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">&#149; </FONT><FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">Based on actual fund return. </FONT><FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">This section helps you to estimate the actual expenses that you paid over the period. The &#148;Ending Account Value&#147; shown is derived from the fund&#145;s actual return, and the third column shows the dollar amount that would have been paid by an investor who started with &#36;1,000 in the fund. You may use the information here, together with the amount you invested, to estimate the expenses that you paid over the period.</FONT></P>
<P style="text-align: left;">
<FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">To do so, simply divide your account value by &#36;1,000 (for example, an &#36;8,600 account value divided by &#36;1,000 = 8.6), then multiply the result by the number given for your fund under the heading &#148;Expenses Paid During Period.&#147;</FONT></P>
<P style="text-align: left;">
<FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">&#149; </FONT><FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">Based on hypothetical 5% yearly return. </FONT><FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">This section is intended to help you compare your fund&#145;s costs with those of other mutual funds. It assumes that the fund had a yearly return of 5% before expenses, but that the expense ratio is unchanged. In this case&#151;because the return used is not the fund&#146;s actual return&#151;the results do not apply to your investment. The example is useful in making comparisons because the Securities and Exchange Commission requires all mutual funds to calculate expenses based on a 5% return. You can assess your fund&#146;s costs by comparing this hypothetical example with the hypothetical examples that appear in shareholder reports of other funds.</FONT></P>
<P style="text-align: left;">
<FONT size=1 face="Univers-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">Note that the expenses shown in the table are meant to highlight and help you compare </FONT><I><FONT size=1 face="Univers-LightOblique,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">ongoing </FONT></I><FONT size=1 face="Univers-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">costs only and do not reflect transaction costs incurred by the fund for buying and selling securities. Further, the expenses do not include any purchase, redemption, or account service fees described in the fund prospectus. If such fees were applied to your account, your costs would be higher. Your fund does not carry a &#147;sales load.&#148;</FONT></P>
<P style="text-align: left;">
<FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">The calculations assume no shares were bought or sold during the period. Your actual costs may have been higher or lower, depending on the amount of your investment and the timing of any purchases or redemptions.</FONT></P>
<P style="text-align: left;">
<FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">You can find more information about the fund&#146;s expenses, including annual expense ratios, in the Financial Statements section of this report. For additional information on operating expenses and other shareholder costs, please refer to your fund&#146;s current prospectus.</FONT></P>

	<TD align=right style="border-bottom:1px solid #000000;">
<FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">0.46</FONT></TD>
</TR>
</TABLE>
</DIV>
<P style="MARGIN:0px">&nbsp;</P>
<P style="text-align: left;">
<FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-LightCn,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">The calculations are based on expenses incurred in the most recent six-month period. The funds&#146; annualized six-month expense ratios for that period are: for the Growth Index Fund, 0.23% for Investor Shares, 0.09% for Admiral Shares, 0.08% for Institutional Shares, and 0.09% for ETF Shares; for the Value Index Fund, 0.23% for Investor Shares, 0.09% for Admiral Shares, 0.08% for Institutional Shares, and 0.09% for ETF Shares; and for the Large-Cap Index Fund, 0.23% for Investor Shares, 0.09% for Admiral Shares, 0.08% for Institutional Shares, and 0.09% for ETF Shares. The dollar amounts shown as &#147;Expenses Paid&#148; are equal to the annualized expense ratio multiplied by the average account value over the period, multiplied by the number of days in the most recent six-month period, then divided by the number of days in the most recent 12-month period.</FONT></P>
<P style="text-align: left;">
<FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">84</FONT></P>

<DIV STYLE="page-break-before: always">&nbsp;</div>



<!--$$/page=-->
<A name="page_330"></A><BR>

<a name="_bclPageBorder330"></a><DIV STYLE="WIDTH: 100%; PADDING-RIGHT: 0%; PADDING-LEFT: 0%">
<P style="text-align: left;">
<FONT size=3 face="UniversLTStd,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">Glossary</FONT></P>
<P style="text-align: left;">
<FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">30-Day SEC Yield. </FONT><FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">A fund&#146;s 30-day SEC yield is derived using a formula specified by the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission. Under the formula, data related to the fund&#146;s security holdings in the previous 30 days are used to calculate the fund&#146;s hypothetical net income for that period, which is then annualized and divided by the fund&#146;s estimated average net assets over the calculation period. For the purposes of this calculation, a security&#146;s income is based on its current market yield to maturity (for bonds), its actual income (for asset-backed securities), or its projected dividend yield (for stocks). Because the SEC yield represents hypothetical annualized income, it will differ&#151;at times significantly&#151;from the fund&#146;s actual experience. As a result, the fund&#146;s income distributions may be higher or lower than implied by the SEC yield.</FONT></P>
<P style="text-align: left;">
<FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">Beta. </FONT><FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">A measure of the magnitude of a fund&#146;s past share-price fluctuations in relation to the ups and downs of a given market index. The index is assigned a beta of 1.00. Compared with a given index, a fund with a beta of 1.20 typically would have seen its share price rise or fall by 12% when the index rose or fell by 10%. For this report, beta is based on returns over the past 36 months for both the fund and the index. Note that a fund&#146;s beta should be reviewed in conjunction with its R-squared (see definition). The lower the R-squared, the less correlation there is between the fund and the index, and the less reliable beta is as an indicator of volatility.</FONT></P>
<P style="text-align: left;">
<FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">Dividend Yield. </FONT><FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">Dividend income earned by stocks, expressed as a percentage of the aggregate market value (or of net asset value, for a fund). The yield is determined by dividing the amount of the annual dividends by the aggregate value (or net asset value) at the end of the period. For a fund, the dividend yield is based solely on stock holdings and does not include any income produced by other investments.</FONT></P>
<P style="text-align: left;">
<FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">Earnings Growth Rate. </FONT><FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">The average annual rate of growth in earnings over the past five years for the stocks now in a fund.</FONT></P>
<P style="text-align: left;">
<FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">Equity Exposure. </FONT><FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">A measure that reflects a fund&#146;s investments in stocks and stock futures. Any holdings in short-term reserves are excluded.</FONT></P>
<P style="text-align: left;">
<FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">Expense Ratio. </FONT><FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">A fund&#146;s total annual operating expenses expressed as a percentage of the fund&#146;s average net assets. The expense ratio includes management and administrative expenses, but does not include the transaction costs of buying and selling portfolio securities.</FONT></P>
<P style="text-align: left;">
<FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">Foreign Holdings. </FONT><FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">The percentage of a fund represented by securities or depositary receipts of companies based outside the United States.</FONT></P>
<P style="text-align: left;">
<FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">Inception Date. </FONT><FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">The date on which the assets of a fund (or one of its share classes) are first invested in accordance with the fund&#146;s investment objective. For funds with a subscription period, the inception date is the day after that period ends. Investment performance is measured from the inception date.</FONT></P>
<P style="text-align: left;">
<FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">Median Market Cap. </FONT><FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">An indicator of the size of companies in which a fund invests; the midpoint of market capitalization (market price x shares outstanding) of a fund&#146;s stocks, weighted by the proportion of the fund&#146;s assets invested in each stock. Stocks representing half of the fund&#146;s assets have market capitalizations above the median, and the rest are below it.</FONT></P>
<P style="text-align: left;">
<FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">Price/Book Ratio. </FONT><FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">The share price of a stock divided by its net worth, or book value, per share. For a fund, the weighted average price/book ratio of the stocks it holds.</FONT></P>
<P style="text-align: left;">
<FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">85</FONT></P>
</DIV>

<DIV STYLE="page-break-before: always">&nbsp;</div>



<!--$$/page=-->
<A name="page_331"></A><BR>

<a name="_bclPageBorder331"></a><DIV STYLE="WIDTH: 100%; PADDING-RIGHT: 0%; PADDING-LEFT: 0%">
<P style="text-align: left;">
<FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">Price/Earnings Ratio. </FONT><FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">The ratio of a stock&#146;s current price to its per-share earnings over the past year. For a fund, the weighted average P/E of the stocks it holds. P/E is an indicator of market expectations about corporate prospects; the higher the P/E, the greater the expectations for a company&#146;s future growth.</FONT></P>
<P style="text-align: left;">
<FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">R-Squared. </FONT><FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">A measure of how much of a fund&#146;s past returns can be explained by the returns from the market in general, as measured by a given index. If a fund&#146;s total returns were precisely synchronized with an index&#146;s returns, its R-squared would be 1.00. If the fund&#146;s returns bore no relationship to the index&#146;s returns, its R-squared would be 0. For this report, R-squared is based on returns over the past 36 months for both the fund and the index.</FONT></P>
<P style="text-align: left;">
<FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">Return on Equity. </FONT><FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">The annual average rate of return generated by a company during the past five years for each dollar of shareholder&#146;s equity (net income divided by shareholder&#146;s equity). For a fund, the weighted average return on equity for the companies whose stocks it holds.</FONT></P>
<P style="text-align: left;">
<FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">Short-Term Reserves. </FONT><FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">The percentage of a fund invested in highly liquid, short-term securities that can be readily converted to cash.</FONT></P>
<P style="text-align: left;">
<FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">Turnover Rate. </FONT><FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">An indication of the fund&#146;s trading activity. Funds with high turnover rates incur higher transaction costs and may be more likely to distribute capital gains (which may be taxable to investors). The turnover rate excludes in-kind transactions, which have minimal impact on costs.</FONT></P>
<P style="text-align: left;">
<FONT size=2 face="UniversLTStd,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">Benchmark Information</FONT></P>
<P style="text-align: left;">
<FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">Spliced Growth Index: </FONT><FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">S&amp;P 500 Growth Index (formerly known as the S&amp;P 500/Barra Growth Index) through May 16, 2003;&#160;MSCI US Prime Market Growth Index through April 16, 2013; CRSP US Large Cap Growth Index thereafter.</FONT></P>
<P style="text-align: left;">
<FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">Spliced Large Cap Index: </FONT><FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">MSCI US Prime Market 750 Index through January 30, 2013; CRSP US Large Cap Index thereafter.</FONT></P>
<P style="text-align: left;">
<FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">Spliced Value Index: </FONT><FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">S&amp;P 500 Value Index (formerly known as the S&amp;P 500/Barra Value Index) through May 16, 2003; MSCI US Prime Market Value Index through April 16, 2013; CRSP US Large Cap Value Index thereafter.</FONT></P>
<P style="text-align: left;">
<FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">86</FONT></P>
</DIV>

<FONT size=2 face="Univers,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">The mission continues</FONT></P>
<P style="text-align: left;">
<FONT size=2 face="Univers-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">On May 1, 1975, Vanguard began operations, a fledgling company based on the simple but revolutionary idea that a mutual fund company should be managed solely in the interest of its investors.</FONT></P>
<P style="text-align: left;">
<FONT size=2 face="Univers-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">Four decades later, that revolutionary spirit continues to animate the enterprise. Vanguard remains on a mission to give investors the best chance of investment success.</FONT></P>
<P style="text-align: left;">
<FONT size=2 face="Univers-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">As we mark our 40th anniversary, we thank you for entrusting your assets to Vanguard and giving us the opportunity to help you reach your financial goals in the decades to come.</FONT></P>

<DIV style="PADDING-LEFT: 0%; PADDING-RIGHT: 0%">

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=3 face=UniversLTStd,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>Chairman&#8217;s Letter</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=2 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>Dear Shareholder,</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=2 face=UniversLTStd,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>The broad U.S. stock market cleared several hurdles on its way to another year of strong gains. Several times during 2014, international conflicts and global economic troubles temporarily halted stocks&#8217; momentum. Each decline, however, was followed by another surge forward, and the broad market finished the year near an all-time high.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=2 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>Vanguard Total Stock Market Index Fund, whose mix of growth and value stocks across all market capitalizations provides investors with exposure to the entire U.S. equity market, returned more than 12% for the 12 months ended December 31, 2014. The fund closely tracked the return of its benchmark, the CRSP US Total Market Index, and outpaced the average return of its multi-cap core fund peers by about 3 percentage points.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=2 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>Please note that the fund&#8217;s Signal Shares were converted to Admiral Shares in October 2014 as part of a year-long plan to streamline Vanguard&#8217;s share-class offerings. If you hold Vanguard Total Stock Market Index Fund in a taxable account, you may wish to review the information about after-tax returns that appears later in this report.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=2 face=UniversLTStd,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>U.S. stocks finished strongly for the sixth straight year</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=2 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>U.S. stocks returned nearly 13% for the 12 months ended December 31, 2014, posting gains for the sixth consecutive</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>2</FONT></P></DIV>

<DIV style="PAGE-BREAK-BEFORE: always">&nbsp;</DIV>

<!--$$/page=--><A name="page_340"></A><BR>

<DIV style="PADDING-LEFT: 0%; PADDING-RIGHT: 0%">

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=2 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>calendar year. Rising corporate earnings, the growing U.S. economy, and generally accommodative global monetary policies lifted domestic markets even as Europe and China faced economic challenges, tensions flared in the Middle East and Ukraine, and concerns arose over stocks&#8217; high valuations.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=2 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>Although the Federal Reserve ended its stimulative bond-buying program in October, investors seemed to be reassured by the Fed&#8217;s stance that it will be &#8220;patient&#8221; as it decides when to increase short-term interest rates. Other central banks&#8212;including the Bank of Japan, the European Central Bank, and the People&#8217;s Bank of China&#8212;also announced significant stimulus measures.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=2 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>International stocks didn&#8217;t fare as well as their U.S. counterparts, returning about &#8211;3% in dollar terms. Their performance was hurt as many foreign currencies weakened against the U.S. dollar. Emerging-market stocks rose slightly, while stocks from the developed markets of Europe and the Pacific region retreated.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=2 face=UniversLTStd,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>Defying analysts&#8217; expectations, bond prices rose during the period</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=2 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>Bond prices received a boost from moves by many of the world&#8217;s central banks along with various global economic, market, and geopolitical challenges that drew investors to perceived safe havens. In an unexpected rebound from the previous year, the broad U.S. bond market returned 5.97% for the period.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=2 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>Even with the Fed&#8217;s paring back of its bond purchases, prices climbed and yields fell. (Bond prices and yields move in opposite directions.) The yield of the 10-year Treasury note ended December at 2.19%, down from 2.97% at the close of December 2013.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=2 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>Municipal bonds returned 9.05%, benefiting from increased demand and generally limited supply.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=2 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>International bond markets (as measured by the Barclays Global Aggregate Index ex USD) returned &#8211;3.08%.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=2 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>As for money market funds and savings accounts, their returns remained minuscule, as the Fed&#8217;s target for short-term interest rates remained between 0% and 0.25%.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=2 face=UniversLTStd,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>Returns were generally strong, with some notable exceptions</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=2 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>Overall the fund&#8217;s performance was positive for 2014. While growth and value stocks performed within a tight range, large- and mid-cap stocks surpassed small-caps by a wide margin. Sector returns ranged from as high as about 26% for both health care and utilities to as low as about &#8211;10% for the oil and gas sector.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=2 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>Health care, one of the fund&#8217;s larger sectors, added the most to overall results. The industry generally profited as investors anticipated a rise in spending given the aging population and the expanded number of insured under the Affordable Care Act, although there are still concerns about the effects of regulation on the managed care industry.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=2 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>New product development, mergers and acquisitions, and strategic alliances have boosted pharmaceutical and biotechnology companies, although the latter endured some turbulence related to high valuations earlier in the year. Innovative new products and therapies helped medical care equipment firms, and health care providers with diverse membership bases and business lines thrived.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=2 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>Technology stocks also powered the fund&#8217;s return. Most segments within the sector appreciated, with hardware and semiconductor companies leading the way as demand for the smartphone, mobile technologies, and cloud-based computing grew in the United States and overseas. Results for internet companies were mixed but still positive as the race for advertising dollars and new products continued to evolve and unfold.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=2 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>The financial sector, the fund&#8217;s largest, was another key to the fund&#8217;s success this year. Low interest rates and the expanding economy propelled real estate investment trusts (REITs) to returns close to 30%. This favorable environment also lifted financial services firms, banks, and insurance firms.</FONT></P>

<DIV style="PADDING-LEFT: 0%; PADDING-RIGHT: 0%">

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=2 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>Increased consumer spending lifted the economy as well as the consumer services and consumer goods sectors. The utilities sector, often unheralded, was a stalwart over the period as the severe winter led to increased earnings and low interest rates attracted some investors to utility stocks&#8217; higher yields.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=2 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>Oil and gas stocks were the fund&#8217;s only losing group, while industrials, basic materials, and telecommunications stocks recorded single-digit returns. The entire oil and gas sector has been hurt by the drop</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=2 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>in oil prices. With their profits cut, producers have scaled back on the projects that are the lifeblood of service firms, drillers, and equipment providers.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=2 face=UniversLTStd,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>The fund&#8217;s broad diversification delivered a decade of solid returns</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=2 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>At Vanguard, we believe in being straightforward with our investors. That includes truth in labeling, which is why the name of your fund is so appropriate. It&#8217;s designed to reflect the performance of the entire U.S. stock market&#8211;&#8211;all sectors, styles, and sizes. There will always be areas that</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=2 face=UniversLTStd,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>Vanguard&#8217;s outlook for investors: Expect less and stay balanced</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>In Vanguard&#8217;s recently published market outlook, global chief economist Joe Davis and his team discuss expected returns for various asset classes over the coming years. Although not bearish, our outlook on global stocks and bonds is the most guarded since 2006. The report cautions that, over the next decade, returns for a balanced portfolio are likely to be moderately below long-run historical averages.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>Our simulations indicate that the average annualized returns of a 60% equity/40% bond portfolio for the decade ending 2024 are most likely to be centered in the 3%&#8211;5% range after inflation, below the actual average after-inflation return of 5.6% for the same portfolio since 1926.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>Even so, Vanguard firmly believes that the principles for investing success&#8212;focusing on clear goals, a suitable asset allocation, low costs, and long-term discipline&#8212;remain unchanged.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>For more information about our expectations and the probability of various outcomes, see </FONT><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-LightObl,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>Vanguard&#8217;s Economic and Investment Outlook</FONT><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>, available at vanguard.com/research.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Cn,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>IMPORTANT: The projections and other information generated by the Vanguard Capital Markets Model (VCMM) regarding the likelihood of various investment outcomes are hypothetical in nature, do not reflect actual investment results, and are not guarantees of future results. Distribution of return outcomes from VCMM, derived from 10,000 simulations for U.S. equity returns and fixed income returns. Simulations as of September 30, 2014. Results from the model may vary with each use and over time. For more information, please see page 7.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>6</FONT></P></DIV>

<DIV style="PAGE-BREAK-BEFORE: always">&nbsp;</DIV>

<!--$$/page=--><A name="page_344"></A><BR>

<DIV style="PADDING-LEFT: 0%; PADDING-RIGHT: 0%">

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=2 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>outperform and underperform the broad market, and your fund&#8217;s mandate is to include them all rather than engage in the challenging, and often disappointing, business of trying to predict the standouts.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=2 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>The fund&#8217;s broad diversification can benefit investors when market returns are relatively balanced across market-capitalization and style segments, and also when they&#8217;re not. The likelihood of this dynamic playing out successfully increases over time as market leaders and laggards inevitably shuffle.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=2 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>Over the past ten years, Investor Shares of Vanguard Total Stock Market Index Fund have produced an average annual return of about 8%, more than 1 percentage point higher than the average return of its peer </FONT><FONT size=2 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>group. Consistent with its objective, the fund tightly tracked its benchmark index over that period. The fund&#8217;s success in staying close to its target index is a testament to the skill of its advisor, the Equity Investment Group. The group relies on its proven portfolio management strategies to produce benchmark-tracking returns regardless of external market conditions. At the same time, of course, the fund&#8217;s low costs help you keep more of the market&#8217;s returns.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=2 face=UniversLTStd,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>To build for the long term, start with a solid foundation</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=2 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>As the leader of a major investment firm, I get asked a lot of questions on all kinds of topics, from the outlook for global markets to the best fund choices for an IRA. But a</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Cn,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>IMPORTANT: The projections and other information generated by the Vanguard Capital Markets Model regarding the likelihood of various investment outcomes are hypothetical in nature, do not reflect actual investment results, and are not guarantees of future results. VCMM results will vary with each use and over time.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-LightCn,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>The VCMM projections are based on a statistical analysis of historical data. Future returns may behave differently from the historical patterns captured in the VCMM. More important, the VCMM may be underestimating extreme negative scenarios unobserved in the historical period on which the model estimation is based.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-LightCn,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>The Vanguard Capital Markets Model</FONT><SUP><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-LightCn,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>&#174; </FONT></SUP><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-LightCn,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>is a proprietary financial simulation tool developed and maintained by Vanguard&#8217;s primary investment research and advice teams. The model forecasts distributions of future returns for a wide array of broad asset classes. Those asset classes include U.S. and international equity markets, several maturities of the U.S. Treasury and corporate fixed income markets, international fixed income markets, U.S. money markets, commodities, and certain alternative investment strategies. The theoretical and empirical foundation for the Vanguard Capital Markets Model is that the returns of various asset classes reflect the compensation investors require for bearing different types of systematic risk (beta). At the core of the model are estimates of the dynamic statistical relationship between risk factors and asset returns, obtained from statistical analysis based on available monthly financial and economic data from as early as 1960. Using a system of estimated equations, the model then applies a Monte Carlo simulation method to project the estimated interrelationships among risk factors and asset classes as well as uncertainty and randomness over time. The model generates a large set of simulated outcomes for each asset class over several time horizons. Forecasts are obtained by computing measures of central tendency in these simulations. Results produced by the tool will vary with each use and over time.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>7</FONT></P></DIV>

<DIV style="PAGE-BREAK-BEFORE: always">&nbsp;</DIV>

<A name="page_345"></A><BR>

<a name="_bclPageBorder345"></a><DIV STYLE="WIDTH: 100%; PADDING-RIGHT: 0%; PADDING-LEFT: 0%">
<P style="text-align: left;">
<FONT size=2 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">topic that almost never comes up&#151;and one that I consider perhaps the most important&#151;is setting investment goals.</FONT></P>
<P style="text-align: left;">
<FONT size=2 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">At Vanguard, we believe that following four timeless, straightforward principles can help put you on the right track toward investment success:</FONT></P>
<P style="text-align: left;">
<FONT size=2 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">&#149; </FONT><FONT size=2 face="UniversLTStd,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">Goals. </FONT><FONT size=2 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">Create clear, appropriate investment goals.</FONT></P>
<P style="text-align: left;">
<FONT size=2 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">&#149; </FONT><FONT size=2 face="UniversLTStd,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">Balance. </FONT><FONT size=2 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">Develop a suitable asset allocation using broadly diversified funds.</FONT></P>
<P style="text-align: left;">
<FONT size=2 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">&#149; </FONT><FONT size=2 face="UniversLTStd,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">Cost. </FONT><FONT size=2 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">Minimize cost.</FONT></P>
<P style="text-align: left;">
<FONT size=2 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">&#149; </FONT><FONT size=2 face="UniversLTStd,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">Discipline. </FONT><FONT size=2 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">Maintain perspective and long-term discipline.</FONT></P>
<P style="text-align: left;">
<FONT size=2 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">All four principles are essential, and the order in which they&#146;re listed is intentional. Every good investment plan begins with a clearly defined goal, which sets the foundation for building your portfolio. (You can read more about our principles in </FONT><FONT size=2 face="UniversLTStd-LightObl,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">Vanguard&#146;s Principles for Investing Success</FONT><FONT size=2 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">, available at vanguard.com/ research.)</FONT></P>
<P style="text-align: left;">
<FONT size=2 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">Setting an investment goal doesn&#146;t have to be complicated. It can be as simple as saving for retirement or for a child&#146;s college education. Being realistic about your goals&#151;and how to meet them&#151;can help you stick with your investment plan even when times get tough.</FONT></P>
<P style="text-align: left;">
<FONT size=2 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">We&#146;ve recently welcomed a new year, which for many means a new beginning. Now is a perfect time to revisit your investment plan and make any necessary adjustments to help you reach your long-term financial goals.</FONT></P>
<P style="text-align: left;">
<FONT size=2 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">As always, thank you for investing with Vanguard.</FONT></P>

<A name="page_361"></A><BR>

<a name="_bclPageBorder361"></a><DIV STYLE="WIDTH: 100%; PADDING-RIGHT: 0%; PADDING-LEFT: 0%">
<P style="text-align: left;">
<FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">Total Stock Market Index Fund</FONT></P>
<P style="text-align: left;">
<FONT size=3 face="UniversLTStd,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">Notes to Financial Statements</FONT></P>
<P style="text-align: left;">
<FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">Vanguard Total Stock Market Index Fund is registered under the Investment Company Act of 1940 as an open-end investment company, or mutual fund. The fund offers four classes of shares: Investor Shares, Admiral Shares, Institutional Shares, and ETF Shares. Investor Shares are available to any investor who meets the fund&#146;s minimum purchase requirements. Admiral Shares and Institutional Shares are designed for investors who meet certain administrative, service, and account-size criteria. ETF Shares are listed for trading on NYSE Arca; they can be purchased and sold through a broker. Prior to October 24, 2014, the fund offered Signal Shares. Effective at the close of business on October 24, 2014, the Signal Shares were converted to Admiral Shares.</FONT></P>
<P style="text-align: left;">
<FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">A. </FONT><FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">The following significant accounting policies conform to generally accepted accounting principles for U.S. investment companies. The fund consistently follows such policies in preparing its financial statements.</FONT></P>
<P style="text-align: left;">
<FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">1. Security Valuation: Securities are valued as of the close of trading on the New York Stock Exchange (generally 4 p.m., Eastern time) on the valuation date. Equity securities are valued at the latest quoted sales prices or official closing prices taken from the primary market in which each security trades; such securities not traded on the valuation date are valued at the mean of the latest quoted bid and asked prices. Securities for which market quotations are not readily available, or whose values have been materially affected by events occurring before the fund&#146;s pricing time but after the close of the securities&#146; primary markets, are valued by methods deemed by the board of trustees to represent fair value. Investments in Vanguard Market Liquidity Fund are valued at that fund&#146;s net asset value. Temporary cash investments acquired over 60 days to maturity are valued using the latest bid prices or using valuations based on a matrix system (which considers such factors as security prices, yields, maturities, and ratings), both as furnished by independent pricing services. Other temporary cash investments are valued at amortized cost, which approximates market value.</FONT></P>
<P style="text-align: left;">
<FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">2. Futures Contracts: The fund uses index futures contracts to a limited extent, with the objectives of maintaining full exposure to the stock market, enhancing returns, maintaining liquidity, and minimizing transaction costs. The fund may purchase futures contracts to immediately invest incoming cash in the market, or sell futures in response to cash outflows, thereby simulating a fully invested position in the underlying index while maintaining a cash balance for liquidity. The fund may seek to enhance returns by using futures contracts instead of the underlying securities when futures are believed to be priced more attractively than the underlying securities. The primary risks associated with the use of futures contracts are imperfect correlation between changes in market values of stocks held by the fund and the prices of futures contracts, and the possibility of an illiquid market. Counterparty risk involving futures is mitigated because a regulated clearinghouse is the counterparty instead of the clearing broker. To further mitigate counterparty risk, the fund trades futures contracts on an exchange, monitors the financial strength of its clearing brokers and clearinghouse, and has entered into clearing agreements with its clearing brokers. The clearinghouse imposes initial margin requirements to secure the fund&#146;s performance and requires daily settlement of variation margin representing changes in the market value of each contract.</FONT></P>
<P style="text-align: left;">
<FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">Futures contracts are valued at their quoted daily settlement prices. The aggregate settlement values of the contracts are not recorded in the Statement of Net Assets. Fluctuations in the value of the contracts are recorded in the Statement of Net Assets as an asset (liability) and in the Statement of Operations as unrealized appreciation (depreciation) until the contracts are closed, when they are recorded as realized futures gains (losses).</FONT></P>
<P style="text-align: left;">
<FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">24</FONT></P>
</DIV>

<DIV STYLE="page-break-before: always">&nbsp;</div>



<!--$$/page=-->
<A name="page_362"></A><BR>

<a name="_bclPageBorder362"></a><DIV STYLE="WIDTH: 100%; PADDING-RIGHT: 0%; PADDING-LEFT: 0%">
<P style="text-align: left;">
<FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">Total Stock Market Index Fund</FONT></P>
<P style="text-align: left;">
<FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">During the year ended December 31, 2014, the fund&#146;s average investments in long and short futures contracts represented less than 1% and 0% of net assets, respectively, based on the average of aggregate settlement values at each quarter-end during the period.</FONT></P>
<P style="text-align: left;">
<FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">3. Swap Contracts: The fund has entered into equity swap contracts to earn the total return on selected reference stocks in the fund&#146;s target index. Under the terms of the swaps, the fund receives the total return on the referenced stock (i.e., receiving the increase or paying the decrease in value of the selected reference stock and receiving the equivalent of any dividends in respect of the selected referenced stock) over a specified period of time, applied to a notional amount that represents the value of a designated number of shares of the selected reference stock at the beginning of the equity swap contract. The fund also pays a floating rate that is based on short-term interest rates, applied to the notional amount. At the same time, the fund invests an amount approximating the notional amount of the swap in high-quality temporary cash investments.</FONT></P>
<P style="text-align: left;">
<FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">The notional amounts of swap contracts are not recorded in the Statement of Net Assets. Swaps are valued daily based on market quotations received from independent pricing services or recognized dealers and the change in value is recorded in the Statement of Net Assets as an asset (liability) and in the Statement of Operations as unrealized appreciation (depreciation) until termination of the swap, at which time realized gain (loss) is recorded. A risk associated with all types of swaps is the possibility that a counterparty may default on its obligation to pay net amounts due to the fund. The fund&#146;s maximum amount subject to counterparty risk is the unrealized appreciation on the swap contract. The fund mitigates its counterparty risk by entering into swaps only with a diverse group of pre-qualified counterparties, monitoring their financial strength, entering into master netting arrangements with its counterparties, and requiring its counterparties to transfer collateral as security for their performance. In the event of a counterparty&#146;s default (including bankruptcy), the fund may terminate any swap contracts with that counterparty, determine the net amount owed by either party in accordance with its master netting arrangements, and sell or retain any collateral held up to the net amount owed to the fund under the master netting arrangements. The swap contracts contain provisions whereby a counterparty may terminate open contracts if the fund net assets decline below a certain level, triggering a payment by the fund if the fund is in a net liability position at the time of the termination. The payment amount would be reduced by any collateral the fund has pledged. Any securities pledged as collateral for open contracts are noted in the Statement of Net Assets. The value of collateral received or pledged is compared daily to the value of the swap contracts exposure with each counterparty, and any difference, if in excess of a specified minimum transfer amount, is adjusted and settled within two business days.</FONT></P>
<P style="text-align: left;">
<FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">During the year ended December 31, 2014, the fund&#146;s average amounts of total return swaps represented less than 1% of net assets, based on the average of notional amounts at each quarter-end during the period.</FONT></P>
<P style="text-align: left;">
<FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">4. Federal Income Taxes: The fund intends to continue to qualify as a regulated investment company and distribute all of its taxable income. Management has analyzed the fund&#146;s tax positions taken for all open federal income tax years (December 31, 2011&#150;2014), and has concluded that no provision for federal income tax is required in the fund&#146;s financial statements.</FONT></P>
<P style="text-align: left;">
<FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">5. Distributions: Distributions to shareholders are recorded on the ex-dividend date.</FONT></P>
<P style="text-align: left;">
<FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">6. Securities Lending: To earn additional income, the fund lends its securities to qualified institutional borrowers. Security loans are required to be secured at all times by collateral in an amount at least equal to the market value of securities loaned. Daily market fluctuations could cause the value of loaned securities to be more or less than the value of the collateral received. When this occurs, the</FONT></P>
<P style="text-align: left;">
<FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">25</FONT></P>
</DIV>

<DIV STYLE="page-break-before: always">&nbsp;</div>



<!--$$/page=-->
<A name="page_363"></A><BR>

<a name="_bclPageBorder363"></a><DIV STYLE="WIDTH: 100%; PADDING-RIGHT: 0%; PADDING-LEFT: 0%">
<P style="text-align: left;">
<FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">Total Stock Market Index Fund</FONT></P>
<P style="text-align: left;">
<FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">collateral is adjusted and settled on the next business day. The fund further mitigates its counterparty risk by entering into securities lending transactions only with a diverse group of prequalified counter-parties, monitoring their financial strength, and entering into master securities lending agreements with its counterparties. The master securities lending agreements provide that, in the event of a counterparty&#146;s default (including bankruptcy), the fund may terminate any loans with that borrower, determine the net amount owed, and sell or retain the collateral up to the net amount owed to the fund; however, such actions may be subject to legal proceedings. While collateral mitigates counter-party risk, in the absence of a default the fund may experience delays and costs in recovering the securities loaned. The fund invests cash collateral received in Vanguard Market Liquidity Fund, and records a liability in the Statement of Net Assets for the return of the collateral, during the period the securities are on loan. Securities lending income represents fees charged to borrowers plus income earned on invested cash collateral, less expenses associated with the loan.</FONT></P>
<P style="text-align: left;">
<FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">7</FONT><FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">. Credit Facility: The fund and certain other funds managed by The Vanguard Group participate in a &#36;2.</FONT><FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">8</FONT><FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">9 billion committed credit facility provided by a syndicate of lenders pursuant to a credit agreement that may be renewed annually; each fund is individually liable for its borrowings, if any, under the credit facility. Borrowings may be utilized for temporary and emergency purposes, and are subject to the fund&#146;s regulatory and contractual borrowing restrictions. The participating funds are charged administrative fees and an annual commitment fee of 0.06% of the undrawn amount of the facility; these fees are allocated to the funds based on a method approved by the fund&#146;s board of trustees and included in Management and Administrative expenses on the fund&#146;s Statement of Operations. Any borrowings under this facility bear interest at a rate equal to the higher of the federal funds rate or LIBOR reference rate plus an agreed-upon spread.</FONT></P>
<P style="text-align: left;">
<FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">The fund had no borrowings outstanding at December 31, 2014, or at any time during the period then ended.</FONT></P>
<P style="text-align: left;">
<FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">8</FONT><FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">. Other: Dividend income is recorded on the ex-dividend date. Interest income includes income distributions received from Vanguard Market Liquidity Fund and is accrued daily. Premiums and discounts on debt securities purchased are amortized and accreted, respectively, to interest income over the lives of the respective securities. Security transactions are accounted for on the date securities are bought or sold. Costs used to determine realized gains (losses) on the sale of investment securities are those of the specific securities sold.</FONT></P>
<P style="text-align: left;">
<FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">Each class of shares has equal rights as to assets and earnings, except that each class separately bears certain class-specific expenses related to maintenance of shareholder accounts (included in Management and Administrative expenses) and shareholder reporting. Marketing and distribution expenses are allocated to each class of shares based on a method approved by the board of trustees. Income, other non-class-specific expenses, and gains and losses on investments are allocated to each class of shares based on its relative net assets.</FONT></P>
<P style="text-align: left;">
<FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">B. </FONT><FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">The Vanguard Group furnishes at cost investment advisory, corporate management, administrative, marketing, and distribution services. The costs of such services are allocated to the fund based on methods approved by the board of trustees. The fund has committed to invest up to 0.40% of its net assets in Vanguard. At December 31, 2014, the fund had contributed capital of &#36;36,11</FONT><FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">7</FONT><FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">,000 to Vanguard (included in Other Assets), representing 0.01% of the fund&#146;s net assets and 14.44% of Vanguard&#146;s capitalization. The fund&#146;s trustees and officers are also directors and officers of Vanguard.</FONT></P>

<P style="MARGIN:0px">&nbsp;</P>
<P style="text-align: left;">
<FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">At December 31, 2014, the counterparty had deposited in segregated accounts securities with a value of &#36;2,608,000 in connection with amounts due to the fund for open swap contracts.</FONT></P>
<P style="text-align: left;">
<FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">E. </FONT><FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">Distributions are determined on a tax basis and may differ from net investment income and realized capital gains for financial reporting purposes. Differences may be permanent or temporary. Permanent differences are reclassified among capital accounts in the financial statements to reflect their tax character. Temporary differences arise when certain items of income, expense, gain, or loss are recognized in different periods for financial statement and tax purposes. These differences will reverse at some time in the future. Differences in classification may also result from the treatment of short-term gains as ordinary income for tax purposes.</FONT></P>
<P style="text-align: left;">
<FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">Certain of the fund&#146;s investments are in securities considered to be passive foreign investment companies, for which any unrealized appreciation and/or realized gains are required to be included in distributable net investment income for tax purposes. During the year ended December 31, 2014, the fund realized gains on the sale of passive foreign investment companies of &#36;54,000, which have been included in current and prior periods&#146; taxable income; accordingly, such gains have been reclassified from accumulated net realized losses to overdistributed net investment income. Passive foreign investment companies had unrealized appreciation of &#36;9,477,000 at December 31, 2014, of which &#36;7,117,000 has been distributed and is reflected in the balance of undistributed net investment income.</FONT></P>
<P style="text-align: left;">
<FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">During the year ended December 31, 2014, the fund realized &#36;4,323,687,000 of net capital gains resulting from in-kind redemptions&#151;in which shareholders exchanged fund shares for securities held by the fund rather than for cash. Because such gains are not taxable to the fund, and are not distributed to shareholders, they have been reclassified from accumulated net realized losses to paid-in capital.</FONT></P>
<P style="text-align: left;">
<FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">Realized and unrealized gains (losses) on certain of the fund&#146;s swap contracts are treated as ordinary income (loss) for tax purposes. Realized losses of &#36;4,133,000 on swap contracts have been reclassified from accumulated net realized losses to overdistributed net investment income.</FONT></P>

<P style="text-align: left;">
<FONT size=3 face="UniversLTStd,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">About Your Fund&#146;s Expenses</FONT></P>
<P style="text-align: left;">
<FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">As a shareholder of the fund, you incur ongoing costs, which include costs for portfolio management, administrative services, and shareholder reports (like this one), among others. Operating expenses, which are deducted from a fund&#146;s gross income, directly reduce the investment return of the fund.</FONT></P>
<P style="text-align: left;">
<FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">A fund&#146;s expenses are expressed as a percentage of its average net assets. This figure is known as the expense ratio. The following examples are intended to help you understand the ongoing costs (in dollars) of investing in your fund and to compare these costs with those of other mutual funds. The examples are based on an investment of &#36;1,000 made at the beginning of the period shown and held for the entire period.</FONT></P>
<P style="text-align: left;">
<FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">The accompanying table illustrates your fund&#146;s costs in two ways:</FONT></P>
<P style="text-align: left;">
<FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">&#149; </FONT><FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">Based on actual fund return. </FONT><FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">This section helps you to estimate the actual expenses that you paid over the period. The &#148;Ending Account Value&#147; shown is derived from the fund&#145;s actual return, and the third column shows the dollar amount that would have been paid by an investor who started with &#36;1,000 in the fund. You may use the information here, together with the amount you invested, to estimate the expenses that you paid over the period.</FONT></P>
<P style="text-align: left;">
<FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">To do so, simply divide your account value by &#36;1,000 (for example, an &#36;8,600 account value divided by &#36;1,000 = 8.6), then multiply the result by the number given for your fund under the heading &#148;Expenses Paid During Period.&#147;</FONT></P>
<P style="text-align: left;">
<FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">&#149; </FONT><FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">Based on hypothetical 5% yearly return. </FONT><FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">This section is intended to help you compare your fund&#145;s costs with those of other mutual funds. It assumes that the fund had a yearly return of 5% before expenses, but that the expense ratio is unchanged. In this case&#151;because the return used is not the fund&#146;s actual return&#151;the results do not apply to your investment. The example is useful in making comparisons because the Securities and Exchange Commission requires all mutual funds to calculate expenses based on a 5% return. You can assess your fund&#146;s costs by comparing this hypothetical example with the hypothetical examples that appear in shareholder reports of other funds.</FONT></P>
<P style="text-align: left;">
<FONT size=1 face="Univers-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">Note that the expenses shown in the table are meant to highlight and help you compare </FONT><I><FONT size=1 face="Univers-LightOblique,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">ongoing </FONT></I><FONT size=1 face="Univers-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">costs only and do not reflect transaction costs incurred by the fund for buying and selling securities. Further, the expenses do not include any purchase, redemption, or account service fees described in the fund prospectus. If such fees were applied to your account, your costs would be higher. Your fund does not carry a &#147;sales load.&#148;</FONT></P>
<P style="text-align: left;">
<FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">The calculations assume no shares were bought or sold during the period. Your actual costs may have been higher or lower, depending on the amount of your investment and the timing of any purchases or redemptions.</FONT></P>
<P style="text-align: left;">
<FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">You can find more information about the fund&#146;s expenses, including annual expense ratios, in the Financial Statements section of this report. For additional information on operating expenses and other shareholder costs, please refer to your fund&#146;s current prospectus.</FONT></P>

<A name="page_372"></A><BR>

<a name="_bclPageBorder372"></a><DIV STYLE="WIDTH: 100%; PADDING-RIGHT: 0%; PADDING-LEFT: 0%">
<P style="text-align: left;">
<FONT size=3 face="UniversLTStd,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">Glossary</FONT></P>
<P style="text-align: left;">
<FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">30-Day SEC Yield. </FONT><FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">A fund&#146;s 30-day SEC yield is derived using a formula specified by the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission. Under the formula, data related to the fund&#146;s security holdings in the previous 30 days are used to calculate the fund&#146;s hypothetical net income for that period, which is then annualized and divided by the fund&#146;s estimated average net assets over the calculation period. For the purposes of this calculation, a security&#146;s income is based on its current market yield to maturity (for bonds), its actual income (for asset-backed securities), or its projected dividend yield (for stocks). Because the SEC yield represents hypothetical annualized income, it will differ&#151;at times significantly&#151;from the fund&#146;s actual experience. As a result, the fund&#146;s income distributions may be higher or lower than implied by the SEC yield.</FONT></P>
<P style="text-align: left;">
<FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">Beta. </FONT><FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">A measure of the magnitude of a fund&#146;s past share-price fluctuations in relation to the ups and downs of a given market index. The index is assigned a beta of 1.00. Compared with a given index, a fund with a beta of 1.20 typically would have seen its share price rise or fall by 12% when the index rose or fell by 10%. For this report, beta is based on returns over the past 36 months for both the fund and the index. Note that a fund&#146;s beta should be reviewed in conjunction with its R-squared (see definition). The lower the R-squared, the less correlation there is between the fund and the index, and the less reliable beta is as an indicator of volatility.</FONT></P>
<P style="text-align: left;">
<FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">Dividend Yield. </FONT><FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">Dividend income earned by stocks, expressed as a percentage of the aggregate market value (or of net asset value, for a fund). The yield is determined by dividing the amount of the annual dividends by the aggregate value (or net asset value) at the end of the period. For a fund, the dividend yield is based solely on stock holdings and does not include any income produced by other investments.</FONT></P>
<P style="text-align: left;">
<FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">Earnings Growth Rate. </FONT><FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">The average annual rate of growth in earnings over the past five years for the stocks now in a fund.</FONT></P>
<P style="text-align: left;">
<FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">Equity Exposure. </FONT><FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">A measure that reflects a fund&#146;s investments in stocks and stock futures. Any holdings in short-term reserves are excluded.</FONT></P>
<P style="text-align: left;">
<FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">Expense Ratio. </FONT><FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">A fund&#146;s total annual operating expenses expressed as a percentage of the fund&#146;s average net assets. The expense ratio includes management and administrative expenses, but does not include the transaction costs of buying and selling portfolio securities.</FONT></P>
<P style="text-align: left;">
<FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">Foreign Holdings. </FONT><FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">The percentage of a fund represented by securities or depositary receipts of companies based outside the United States.</FONT></P>
<P style="text-align: left;">
<FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">Inception Date. </FONT><FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">The date on which the assets of a fund (or one of its share classes) are first invested in accordance with the fund&#146;s investment objective. For funds with a subscription period, the inception date is the day after that period ends. Investment performance is measured from the inception date.</FONT></P>
<P style="text-align: left;">
<FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">Median Market Cap. </FONT><FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">An indicator of the size of companies in which a fund invests; the midpoint of market capitalization (market price x shares outstanding) of a fund&#146;s stocks, weighted by the proportion of the fund&#146;s assets invested in each stock. Stocks representing half of the fund&#146;s assets have market capitalizations above the median, and the rest are below it.</FONT></P>
<P style="text-align: left;">
<FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">Price/Book Ratio. </FONT><FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">The share price of a stock divided by its net worth, or book value, per share. For a fund, the weighted average price/book ratio of the stocks it holds.</FONT></P>
<P style="text-align: left;">
<FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">35</FONT></P>
</DIV>

<DIV STYLE="page-break-before: always">&nbsp;</div>



<!--$$/page=-->
<A name="page_373"></A><BR>

<a name="_bclPageBorder373"></a><DIV STYLE="WIDTH: 100%; PADDING-RIGHT: 0%; PADDING-LEFT: 0%">
<P style="text-align: left;">
<FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">Price/Earnings Ratio. </FONT><FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">The ratio of a stock&#146;s current price to its per-share earnings over the past year. For a fund, the weighted average P/E of the stocks it holds. P/E is an indicator of market expectations about corporate prospects; the higher the P/E, the greater the expectations for a company&#146;s future growth.</FONT></P>
<P style="text-align: left;">
<FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">R-Squared. </FONT><FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">A measure of how much of a fund&#146;s past returns can be explained by the returns from the market in general, as measured by a given index. If a fund&#146;s total returns were precisely synchronized with an index&#146;s returns, its R-squared would be 1.00. If the fund&#146;s returns bore no relationship to the index&#146;s returns, its R-squared would be 0. For this report, R-squared is based on returns over the past 36 months for both the fund and the index.</FONT></P>
<P style="text-align: left;">
<FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">Return on Equity. </FONT><FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">The annual average rate of return generated by a company during the past five years for each dollar of shareholder&#146;s equity (net income divided by shareholder&#146;s equity). For a fund, the weighted average return on equity for the companies whose stocks it holds.</FONT></P>
<P style="text-align: left;">
<FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">Short-Term Reserves. </FONT><FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">The percentage of a fund invested in highly liquid, short-term securities that can be readily converted to cash.</FONT></P>
<P style="text-align: left;">
<FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">Turnover Rate. </FONT><FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">An indication of the fund&#146;s trading activity. Funds with high turnover rates incur higher transaction costs and may be more likely to distribute capital gains (which may be taxable to investors). The turnover rate excludes in-kind transactions, which have minimal impact on costs.</FONT></P>
<P style="text-align: left;">
<FONT size=2 face="UniversLTStd,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">Benchmark Information</FONT></P>
<P style="text-align: left;">
<FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">Spliced Total Stock Market Index: </FONT><FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">Dow Jones U.S. Total Stock Market Index (formerly known as the Dow Jones Wilshire 5000 Index) through April 22, 2005; MSCI US Broad Market Index through June 2, 2013; and CRSP US Total Market Index thereafter.</FONT></P>
<P style="text-align: left;">
<FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">36</FONT></P>
</DIV>

<P style="text-align: left;">
<FONT size=3 face="UniversLTStd,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">The People Who Govern Your Fund</FONT></P>
<P style="text-align: left;">
<FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">The trustees of your mutual fund are there to see that the fund is operated and managed in your best interests since, as a shareholder, you are a part owner of the fund. Your fund&#146;s trustees also serve on the board of directors of The Vanguard Group, Inc., which is owned by the Vanguard funds and provides services to them on an at-cost basis.</FONT></P>
<P style="text-align: left;">
<FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">A majority of Vanguard&#146;s board members are independent, meaning that they have no affiliation with Vanguard or the funds they oversee, apart from the sizable personal investments they have made as private individuals. The independent board members have distinguished backgrounds in business, academia, and public service. Each of the trustees and executive officers oversees 1</FONT><FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">77 </FONT><FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">Vanguard funds.</FONT></P>
